1	"""tests/hw/test_l3tc_tail_gate.py — per-cell L3-TC conversion gate (owner baseline).
2	
3	The owner baseline directive's per-cell gates for a newly-converted L3-TC cell:
4	  (1) megakernel-vs-eager single-step  — the in-kernel optimizer TAIL must match a
5	      reference apply of the SAME canonical update on the SAME TC-reduced grad.
6	  (2) A/A/A determinism                — the production L3-TC step is bit-identical
7	      across 3 runs from the same init (fixed tile ownership + ascending-k/t reduce).
8	
9	WHY THIS SHAPE (not a full loss-trajectory-vs-eager oracle): the bf16 wgmma fwd+bwd
10	and the deterministic grad reduction are SHARED with the already-gated adamw TC cell
11	(decoder 13/13+5, vit 21/21, mamba 5/5 — grad parity vs the bf16-faithful oracle).
12	A converted cell changes ONLY the per-element tail (apply_optimizer<Opt>), which is
13	the 14/0-apply-parity math. So the cell-specific NEW surface is exactly the tail, and
14	the right gate is "did the kernel's tail apply the canonical update to the reduced
15	grad correctly" — which is (1). The grad itself is validated by the adamw gates +
16	the determinism check (2) proves no race was introduced by the tail swap.
17	
18	The reference apply is the canonical CPU math (transcribed from csrc/algorithms/<opt>.h
19	— the SAME single source the kernel's apply_optimizer<Opt> calls), run on the grad the
20	kernel returns (fused_train_step(return_grad=True)). fp32 both sides → tight tol.
21	
22	Run:
23	  PYTHONPATH=. python -m tests.hw.test_l3tc_tail_gate                 # all converted
24	  PYTHONPATH=. python -m tests.hw.test_l3tc_tail_gate --cell lion/decoder
25	  PYTHONPATH=. python -m pytest tests/hw/test_l3tc_tail_gate.py -q
26	"""
27	from __future__ import annotations
28	
29	import argparse
30	import sys
31	from pathlib import Path
32	
33	import torch
34	
35	ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
36	
37	
38	def _g():
39	    if str(ROOT) not in sys.path:
40	        sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
41	    import grokking_race_v2 as g
42	    return g
43	
44	
45	# Cell spec: model, race optimizer key, and a factory that builds the REAL eager
46	# optimizer with the EXACT production hyperparameters (the SAME ones train_<opt> uses).
47	# The gate references this LIVE optimizer (not a header re-transcription), so it catches
48	# any mechanism the real optimizer has that apply_optimizer<Opt> drops (grad_clip,
49	# per-layer schedules, adaptive alpha) — the "megakernel-vs-REAL-eager" the directive
50	# means. State layout in fused_train_step is [m|v|extra].
51	def _adamw_factory(g, params, c):
52	    # train_adamw: torch.optim.AdamW(lr, betas=(beta1,beta2), weight_decay, fused=True)
53	    import torch
54	    return torch.optim.AdamW(params, lr=c["lr"], betas=(c["beta1"], c["beta2"]),
55	                             weight_decay=c["weight_decay"])
56	
57	
58	def _lion_factory(g, params, c):
59	    # train_lion: Lion(lr=lion_lr, betas=(beta1, 0.99), weight_decay=lion_wd)
60	    return g.Lion(params, lr=c.get("lion_lr", 3e-4), betas=(c["beta1"], 0.99),
61	                  weight_decay=c.get("lion_wd", 3.0))
62	
63	
64	def _grokfast_factory(g, params, c):
65	    # train_grokfast: Grokfast(lr, betas=(beta1,beta2), weight_decay,
66	    #                          grokfast_alpha, grokfast_lamb)
67	    return g.Grokfast(params, lr=c["lr"], betas=(c["beta1"], c["beta2"]),
68	                      weight_decay=c["weight_decay"],
69	                      grokfast_alpha=c.get("grokfast_alpha", 0.98),
70	                      grokfast_lamb=c.get("grokfast_lamb", 2.0))
71	
72	
73	def _grokadamw_factory(g, params, c):
74	    # train_grokadamw: GrokAdamW(lr, betas, weight_decay, alpha, gamma, kappa,
75	    #                            lamb, grad_clip, ...) — has grad_clip + gamma + kappa
76	    return g.GrokAdamW(params, lr=c["lr"], betas=(c["beta1"], c["beta2"]),
77	                       weight_decay=c["weight_decay"],
78	                       alpha=c.get("grokadamw_alpha", 0.98),
79	                       gamma=c.get("grokadamw_gamma", 0.1),
80	                       kappa=c.get("grokadamw_kappa", 0.1),
81	                       lamb=c.get("grokadamw_lamb", 2.0),
82	                       grad_clip=c.get("grokadamw_grad_clip", 1.0))
83	
84	
85	# CONVERTED cells (state-gate clean → production-registered). lion's exp_avg cold-
86	# starts at ZEROS (lion.py), matching the kernel's zero-init state cache, so its tail
87	# AND state match the real optimizer exactly. adamw is included as the REGRESSION
88	# guard for the OptId-generic launcher refactor: the production adamw path now flows
89	# through the same opt_id-switched launcher (opt_id=0) with the unconditional
90	# ema/psi-net binding — this re-validates that change against the real AdamW (params
91	# AND m/v state), which the standalone tc_train_step gates (13/13+5, 21/21) do NOT
92	# cover (they call the cell's own pybind, not the launcher TU dispatch.cpp uses).
93	_CELLS = {
94	    "adamw/decoder": dict(model="decoder", opt="adamw", factory=_adamw_factory),
95	    "adamw/vit":     dict(model="vit",     opt="adamw", factory=_adamw_factory),
96	    "lion/decoder":  dict(model="decoder", opt="lion", factory=_lion_factory),
97	    "lion/vit":      dict(model="vit",     opt="lion", factory=_lion_factory),
98	    # grokfast (cycle 2): the kernel cold-starts ema=grad at step==1
99	    # (apply_optimizer<Grokfast> in opt_components.cuh), matching the eager
100	    # ema=grad0 seed (grokfast.py _group_cache), so the (1b) STATE check now passes
101	    # the ema slice (was rel 0.98 when the kernel inited ema=0). grokfast has no
102	    # grad_clip and _opt_scalars_from forwards grokfast_alpha/lamb, so the live
103	    # optimizer's full mechanism reaches the tail.
104	    "grokfast/decoder": dict(model="decoder", opt="grokfast", factory=_grokfast_factory),
105	    "grokfast/vit":     dict(model="vit",     opt="grokfast", factory=_grokfast_factory),
106	    # mamba (cycle-2 directive (c)): the mamba TC kernel is now wired in-_ops, so the
107	    # same OptId-generic tail runs over the mamba TC-reduced grad. adamw is the
108	    # regression guard for mamba's wgmma launcher (the scalar mamba×adamw path stays
109	    # too); lion/grokfast are the new tails. mamba's wgmma kernel needs B%16==0 —
110	    # fused_train_step truncates the batch (kSeq=8). The cold-start fix applies to
111	    # mamba's P3 identically (apply_optimizer<Grokfast> is model-independent).
112	    "adamw/mamba":    dict(model="mamba", opt="adamw", factory=_adamw_factory),
113	    "lion/mamba":     dict(model="mamba", opt="lion", factory=_lion_factory),
114	    "grokfast/mamba": dict(model="mamba", opt="grokfast", factory=_grokfast_factory),
115	}
116	
117	# BLOCKED cells — kept here (commented) with the state-gate evidence that blocks them,
118	# so the reason is reproducible. NOT registered in _FUSED_L3_REAL; the gate's
119	# has_l3_real precondition would (correctly) refuse to run them as "converted".
120	#  * grokadamw/{decoder,vit}: THREE eager mechanisms a single global FusedScalars
121	#    cannot carry, ALL required (no-suppression): (i) per-tensor layer-wise beta1 =
122	#    beta1·(1-gamma)^layer (gamma=0.1); (ii) per-tensor grad-norm clip to grad_clip=1.0
123	#    (eager grokadamw_fused_step → clip_grad_norms_device_side, bindings.cpp:215); (iii)
124	#    adaptive alpha_t. The single-step gate would HOLLOW-PASS: (ii)+(iii) are inert at
125	#    step 1 (no reduced-grad tensor norm > 1.0 / no losses fed), so registering on a
126	#    green single-step gate would read "converted" while the cell diverges multi-step.
127	#    Needs the per-tensor scalar side-channel (i) + a P3 norm reduction (ii). The ema
128	#    cold-start is already staged in apply_optimizer<GrokAdamW>.
129	_BLOCKED_EVIDENCE = {
130	    "grokadamw/decoder": dict(model="decoder", opt="grokadamw", factory=_grokadamw_factory),
131	    "grokadamw/vit":     dict(model="vit",     opt="grokadamw", factory=_grokadamw_factory),
132	}
133	
134	
135	def _build_cell(model, seed=42):
136	    """Build the live race model + one real batch + the L3-REAL flat layout.
137	
138	    DETERMINISM (load-bearing for gate 2): build_model does NOT reseed from
139	    c["seed"] internally — it draws from the global RNG — so the A/A/A determinism
140	    check MUST reseed here, or each rebuild yields different random init weights and
141	    the gate would compare runs with DIFFERENT inputs (a test bug, not kernel
142	    non-determinism). We torch.manual_seed(seed) immediately before build_model so
143	    every _build_cell(model, seed) returns byte-identical initial params."""
144	    g = _g()
145	    c = dict(g.DEFAULT_CONFIG)
146	    c.update({"model_type": model, "use_amp": False, "use_fused": True,
147	              "compile_model": False, "matmul_precision": "bf16", "seed": seed,
148	              "frac_train": 0.5, "val_ratio": 0.10, "p": 97})
149	    dev = torch.device("cuda")

151	    torch.manual_seed(seed)            # pin build_model's global-RNG draw
152	    torch.cuda.manual_seed_all(seed)

157	def run_cell_gate(cell_key, verbose=True):
158	    """Run gates (1)+(2) for one converted cell. Returns (ok, detail)."""
159	    from grokking_optimizers.dispatch import (has_l3_real, gemm_impl_for_cell,
160	                                              canonicalize_model, fused_train_step)
161	    spec = _CELLS[cell_key]
162	    model, opt = spec["model"], spec["opt"]
163	    g, c, m, data, dev = _build_cell(model)
164	    canon = canonicalize_model(model)
165	    # Precondition: the cell must actually be wired L3-TC (wgmma) — else the gate is
166	    # meaningless. has_l3_real + gemm_impl_for_cell are the production gates.
167	    assert has_l3_real(canon, opt), f"{cell_key}: not L3-REAL (wire it first)"
168	    eng = gemm_impl_for_cell(canon, opt, "bf16")
169	    assert eng == "wgmma", f"{cell_key}: bf16 engine is {eng!r}, expected wgmma"
170	
171	    tx, ty = data[0], data[1]
172	    # A live optimizer carrying the EXACT production hyperparameters (drives the
173	    # kernel's scalars via _opt_scalars_from inside fused_train_step).
174	    opt_obj = spec["factory"](g, m.parameters(), c)
175	
176	    # Snapshot the initial flat params (named_parameters order) BEFORE the step.
177	    named0 = [(n, p) for n, p in m.named_parameters() if p.requires_grad]
178	    total = sum(p.numel() for _, p in named0)
179	    p_before = torch.empty(total, device=dev)
180	    off = 0
181	    for _, p in named0:
182	        n = p.numel(); p_before[off:off + n].copy_(p.data.reshape(-1)); off += n
183	
184	    # ── (1) megakernel-vs-REAL-EAGER single-step: run ONE production L3-TC step (the
185	    # SAME route the race takes), capturing the TC-reduced grad + the post-step
186	    # params. The state cache starts at zero (m=v=extra=0).
187	    cache = {}
188	    loss, grad = fused_train_step(canon, opt, m, opt_obj, tx, ty,
189	                                  state_cache=cache, step=1, return_grad=True,
190	                                  gemm_impl="wgmma")
191	    # params after the kernel step (named order → flat).
192	    p_after = torch.empty(total, device=dev)
193	    off = 0
194	    for _, p in named0:
195	        n = p.numel(); p_after[off:off + n].copy_(p.data.reshape(-1)); off += n
196	
197	    # REFERENCE = the REAL eager optimizer (not a header re-transcription). Build a
198	    # FRESH model with the SAME init (same seed), INJECT the kernel's TC-reduced grad
199	    # into each p.grad (so both sides consume the BYTE-IDENTICAL gradient — the bf16-TC
200	    # grad — isolating the optimizer TAIL math), then run ONE real opt.step() from
201	    # zero state. A mechanism the real optimizer has but apply_optimizer<Opt> drops
202	    # (grad_clip, per-layer schedule, adaptive alpha) SHOWS UP here as a param mismatch.
203	    g_r, c_r, m_ref, data_r, dev_r = _build_cell(model)
204	    named_ref = [(n, p) for n, p in m_ref.named_parameters() if p.requires_grad]
205	    # confirm the fresh model's init matches p_before (same seed) — the reference is
206	    # only valid if it starts from the kernel's input params.
207	    p_ref_before = torch.cat([p.data.reshape(-1) for _, p in named_ref])
208	    assert torch.equal(p_ref_before, p_before), \
209	        f"{cell_key}: reference model init != kernel init (seed mismatch)"
210	    opt_ref = spec["factory"](g_r, m_ref.parameters(), c_r)
211	    # Scatter the kernel's flat TC grad into the reference params' .grad (layout order).
212	    off = 0
213	    for _, p in named_ref:
214	        n = p.numel()
215	        p.grad = grad[off:off + n].reshape(p.shape).clone()
216	        off += n
217	    opt_ref.step()
218	    p_ref = torch.cat([p.data.reshape(-1) for _, p in named_ref])
219	
220	    # The kernel and the real optimizer consumed the SAME grad; the only legitimate
221	    # difference is fp32 rounding order in the elementwise tail. A DROPPED mechanism
222	    # (e.g. grad_clip scaling every grad, or a per-layer beta1) makes this large.
223	    abs_err = (p_after - p_ref).abs().max().item()
224	    denom = p_ref.abs().max().item() + 1e-30
225	    rel_err = abs_err / denom
226	    param_ok = rel_err < 1e-4   # fp32 reorder tol; a dropped mechanism blows past this
227	    if verbose:
228	        print(f"  (1a) params vs REAL eager: max|Δp|={abs_err:.3e} rel={rel_err:.3e} "
229	              f"(tol 1e-4) {'OK' if param_ok else 'FAIL'}  loss={loss:.5f}", flush=True)
230	
231	    # ── (1b) STATE vs REAL eager — THE DECISIVE CHECK. At step 1 every Adam-family
232	    # tail collapses to ≈sign(g_amp) in the PARAM update (m/bc1=g_amp, sqrt(v/bc2)=
233	    # |g_amp|), so (1a) is BLIND to per-layer beta1 (gamma), amplification magnitude,
234	    # and STATE INITIALIZATION — all of which live in the optimizer state, not the
235	    # sign. So we compare the kernel's post-step state slices [m|v|ema] (in the cache
236	    # buffer) against the REAL optimizer's opt.state[p]. A state mismatch == the kernel
237	    # is NOT running the real optimizer (e.g. grokfast's ema cold-start: real inits
238	    # ema=g0, the kernel inits ema=0 → the ema slice diverges 50x even when params
239	    # match). This is what makes the single-step verdict mean "runs the real optimizer".
240	    kstate = cache[canon]["state"]              # flat [m|v|extra] (3*total)+loss
241	    k_m = kstate[0:total]; k_v = kstate[total:2 * total]; k_ema = kstate[2 * total:3 * total]
242	    # Gather the real optimizer's per-parameter state into flat buffers (layout order).
243	    r_m = torch.zeros(total, device=dev); r_v = torch.zeros(total, device=dev)
244	    r_ema = torch.zeros(total, device=dev)
245	    have_v = have_ema = False
246	    off = 0
247	    for _, p in named_ref:
248	        n = p.numel(); stt = opt_ref.state.get(p, {})
249	        if "exp_avg" in stt:
250	            r_m[off:off + n].copy_(stt["exp_avg"].reshape(-1))
251	        if "exp_avg_sq" in stt:
252	            r_v[off:off + n].copy_(stt["exp_avg_sq"].reshape(-1)); have_v = True
253	        if "ema" in stt:
254	            r_ema[off:off + n].copy_(stt["ema"].reshape(-1)); have_ema = True
255	        off += n
256	    def _rel(a, b):
257	        d = (a - b).abs().max().item(); return d / (b.abs().max().item() + 1e-30)
258	    m_rel = _rel(k_m, r_m)
259	    v_rel = _rel(k_v, r_v) if have_v else 0.0
260	    ema_rel = _rel(k_ema, r_ema) if have_ema else None
261	    # The kernel and real opt consumed the SAME grad; their state must match to fp32
262	    # reorder tol. ema only checked when the optimizer HAS an ema buffer.
263	    state_ok = (m_rel < 1e-4 and v_rel < 1e-4
264	                and (ema_rel is None or ema_rel < 1e-4))
265	    if verbose:
266	        ema_s = f"ema={ema_rel:.3e}" if ema_rel is not None else "ema=n/a"
267	        print(f"  (1b) STATE vs REAL eager: m={m_rel:.3e} v={v_rel:.3e} {ema_s} "
268	              f"(tol 1e-4) {'OK' if state_ok else 'FAIL — kernel state != real optimizer'}",
269	              flush=True)
270	    tail_ok = param_ok and state_ok
271	
272	    # ── (2) A/A/A determinism: re-run the production step 3× from the SAME init,
273	    # fresh state each time → loss + grad + params must be BIT-identical.
274	    def _one():
275	        g2, c2, m2, data2, dev2 = _build_cell(model)
276	        tx2, ty2 = data2[0], data2[1]
277	        opt2 = spec["factory"](g2, m2.parameters(), c2)
278	        cc = {}
279	        L, G = fused_train_step(canon, opt, m2, opt2, tx2, ty2, state_cache=cc,
280	                                step=1, return_grad=True, gemm_impl="wgmma")
281	        P = torch.empty(total, device=dev2)
282	        o = 0
283	        for _, p in m2.named_parameters():
284	            if p.requires_grad:
285	                k = p.numel(); P[o:o + k].copy_(p.data.reshape(-1)); o += k
286	        return L, G.clone(), P
287	    L1, G1, P1 = _one(); L2, G2, P2 = _one(); L3, G3, P3 = _one()
288	    det_ok = (L1 == L2 == L3 and torch.equal(G1, G2) and torch.equal(G2, G3)
289	              and torch.equal(P1, P2) and torch.equal(P2, P3))
290	    if verbose:
291	        print(f"  (2) A/A/A determinism: loss {L1:.6f}/{L2:.6f}/{L3:.6f}  "
292	              f"grad-eq={torch.equal(G1,G2) and torch.equal(G2,G3)}  "
293	              f"param-eq={torch.equal(P1,P2) and torch.equal(P2,P3)}  "
294	              f"{'OK' if det_ok else 'FAIL'}", flush=True)
295	    ok = tail_ok and det_ok
296	    return ok, dict(rel_err=rel_err, loss=loss, det=det_ok)

2	path is the L3-TC persistent megakernel (bf16 wgmma engine), fail LOUD otherwise.
3	
4	Mandated by the locked baseline directive: "build a wiring_check.py: route every
5	cell, assert executed path == L3-TC, fail loud — saved to repo, run before every
6	roofline." This is the per-cell pass/fail oracle for the 33 (model × optimizer)
7	cells; the roofline must not be measured until this reports the converted set.
8	
9	WHAT IT DOES (no surrogate, no inference from gate logic — it OBSERVES the real
10	executed engine):
11	  * For each (model, optimizer) cell it runs a few REAL race train steps via the
12	    production train_<opt> function (grokking_race_v2.OPTIMIZER_REGISTRY), with
13	    the SAME dispatch wrapper the roofline uses to capture grokking_race_v2.
14	    LAST_L3_ENGINE — the engine dispatch.cpp ACTUALLY ran ("wgmma" | "scalar" |
15	    None). dispatch.cpp has no silent wgmma->scalar fallback, so a captured
16	    engine=="wgmma" PROVES the bf16 tensor-core L3 megakernel executed.
17	  * A cell PASSES iff every timed step fired engine=="wgmma" (path == L3-TC) AND
18	    the stale-ABI latch never tripped (a TypeError soft-degrade would mean the
19	    extension predates the widened fused_step ABI — rebuild, then re-run).
20	  * A cell is BLOCKED otherwise; the row records the OBSERVED path (eager /
21	    eager+L1-fused-tail / L3-scalar) and a cited reason so the converted/blocked
22	    table is self-documenting.

24	USAGE
25	  python wiring_check.py                       # all 33 cells, table + JSON
26	  python wiring_check.py --models decoder      # subset
27	  python wiring_check.py --opts adamw,lion     # subset
28	  python wiring_check.py --require-all         # exit 1 unless ALL routed cells
29	                                               # are L3-TC (the FULL-baseline gate)
30	Default exit code: 0 if the run completed (the converted/blocked split is the
31	deliverable); --require-all makes a non-fully-converted run fail loud (exit 1),
32	which is the gate the locked directive's end-state wants green.

155	    """Route ONE cell through the real race train fn for `steps` steps and report

159	    g = _g()

161	    data, init = _data_init(model)

164	    # Capture the engine of EVERY L3 step + whether L1 ever fired, by wrapping the
165	    # two dispatch entry points (identical technique to tuning.roofline). We record
166	    # the SET of engines seen across the timed steps so a cell that flickers between
167	    # paths is caught (it must be wgmma on EVERY step to pass).
168	    seen_l3_engines = []
169	    l1_fired = [0]
170	    _orig_l3 = g._try_fused_train_step
171	    _orig_l1 = g._try_fused_step
172	
173	    def _wrap_l3(*a, **k):
174	        r = _orig_l3(*a, **k)
175	        if r is not None:
176	            eng = g.LAST_L3_ENGINE["engine"] if g.LAST_L3_ENGINE else None
177	            seen_l3_engines.append(eng)
178	        return r
179	
180	    def _wrap_l1(*a, **k):
181	        r = _orig_l1(*a, **k)
182	        if r:
183	            l1_fired[0] += 1
184	        return r
185	
186	    g._try_fused_train_step = _wrap_l3
187	    g._try_fused_step = _wrap_l1

193	        torch.cuda.synchronize()

195	        err = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"
196	        traceback.print_exc()

212	    elif n_l3 > 0 and all(e == "scalar" for e in seen_l3_engines):
213	        path = "L3-scalar-megakernel"
214	    elif n_l3 > 0:

216	    elif l1_fired[0] > 0:

223	        reason = ""
224	    elif err is not None:
225	        reason = f"step raised: {err}"
226	    elif abi_stale:
227	        reason = ("ABI-stale latch tripped (extension predates the widened "
228	                  "fused_step signature) — rebuild _ops then re-run.")
229	    elif path == "L3-scalar-megakernel":
230	        reason = ("ran the fp32 SCALAR L3 megakernel, not the bf16 wgmma TC engine. "
231	                  + _MODEL_NOTE.get(model, ""))
232	    else:
233	        # eager / eager+L1: the cell has no production L3-TC route.
234	        # Single-launch wgmma-tail optimizers (lion is the only converted one; the
235	        # others have their own tail-specific blocker) that land on mamba are blocked
236	        # by the MISSING mamba wgmma launcher TU — cite that, not the generic reason.
237	        _wgmma_tails = {"adamw", "lion", "grokfast", "grokadamw", "neuralgrok"}
238	        if model == "mamba" and opt in _wgmma_tails and opt not in _BLOCK_REASONS:
239	            reason = ("BLOCKED by the missing mamba wgmma launcher TU. " + _MODEL_NOTE["mamba"])
240	        else:
241	            reason = _BLOCK_REASONS.get(
242	                opt, "no production L3-TC route wired for this (model, optimizer).")
243	        if model in _MODEL_NOTE and opt == "adamw":
244	            reason = _MODEL_NOTE[model]
245	
246	    return {
247	        "model": model, "optimizer": opt,
248	        "executed_path": path,
249	        "l3_steps_fired": n_l3,
250	        "l3_engines_seen": sorted(set(seen_l3_engines)),
251	        "l1_steps_fired": l1_fired[0],
252	        "abi_stale": abi_stale,
253	        "error": err,
254	        "is_l3_tc": converted,
255	        "reason_if_blocked": reason,
256	    }
257	
258	
259	def main():
260	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
261	    ap.add_argument("--models", default=",".join(MODELS))
262	    ap.add_argument("--opts", default=",".join(OPTS))
263	    ap.add_argument("--steps", type=int, default=4,
264	                    help="real train steps to route per cell (default 4)")
265	    ap.add_argument("--require-all", action="store_true",
266	                    help="exit 1 unless EVERY routed cell executed L3-TC (the "
267	                         "full-baseline gate); default exits 0 with the split")
268	    ap.add_argument("--out", default=str(OUT / "wiring_check.json"))
269	    args = ap.parse_args()
270	    models = [m for m in args.models.split(",") if m]
271	    opts = [o for o in args.opts.split(",") if o]
272	    OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
273	
274	    print(f"[wiring_check] routing {len(models)*len(opts)} cells "
275	          f"({len(models)} models x {len(opts)} opts), {args.steps} real steps each.\n"
276	          f"[wiring_check] PASS == executed engine is wgmma (bf16 TC L3 megakernel) "
277	          f"on EVERY step.\n", flush=True)
278	    rows = []
279	    for model in models:
280	        for opt in opts:
281	            row = check_cell(opt, model, steps=args.steps)
282	            rows.append(row)
283	            mark = "PASS L3-TC" if row["is_l3_tc"] else "BLOCKED   "
284	            extra = "" if row["is_l3_tc"] else f"  ← {row['reason_if_blocked'][:72]}"
285	            print(f"  [{mark}] {opt:11s}/{model:7s}  path={row['executed_path']:26s}"
286	                  f"{extra}", flush=True)
287	
288	    converted = [r for r in rows if r["is_l3_tc"]]
289	    blocked = [r for r in rows if not r["is_l3_tc"]]
290	    n = len(rows)
291	    frac = len(converted) / n if n else 0.0
292	    summary = {
293	        "total_cells": n,
294	        "converted_l3_tc": len(converted),
295	        "blocked": len(blocked),
296	        "fraction_l3_tc": round(frac, 4),
297	        "converted_cells": [f"{r['optimizer']}/{r['model']}" for r in converted],
298	        "blocked_cells": [f"{r['optimizer']}/{r['model']}" for r in blocked],
299	    }
300	    payload = {"summary": summary, "rows": rows}
301	    Path(args.out).write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2))
302	    print(f"\n[wiring_check] {len(converted)}/{n} cells on L3-TC "
303	          f"({100*frac:.1f}%).  wrote {args.out}", flush=True)
304	
305	    # Fraction table by model (the directive's "frac table" seed).
306	    print("\n[wiring_check] L3-TC fraction by model:", flush=True)
307	    for model in models:
308	        mrows = [r for r in rows if r["model"] == model]
309	        c = sum(1 for r in mrows if r["is_l3_tc"])
310	        print(f"   {model:8s}: {c}/{len(mrows)} L3-TC", flush=True)
311	
312	    if args.require_all and blocked:
313	        print(f"\n[wiring_check] FAIL-LOUD (--require-all): {len(blocked)} cell(s) "
314	              f"are NOT L3-TC. The locked baseline requires all 33 on L3-TC. "
315	              f"Blocked: {summary['blocked_cells']}", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
316	        sys.exit(1)
317	    print("\n[wiring_check] DONE", flush=True)
318	
319	
320	if __name__ == "__main__":
321	    main()

1	# Fused-megakernel component contract (portability spec)
2	
3	Owner requirement (2026-06-09): every (model × optimizer × arch) configuration —
4	all 3 models × 11 optimizers — composes into ONE persistent megakernel binary,
5	and the building blocks are **individually portable**: a third project lifts the
6	headers and instantiates a fused trainer without dragging this repo along. The
7	meta-programming lives in headers; the dispatch layer is generated and is the
8	only composition seam.
9	
10	## Component taxonomy (header-only, self-contained)
11	
12	| component | header(s) | contract |
13	|---|---|---|
14	| **Substrate** | `csrc/fused/megakernel_common.cuh` | `PersistentContext` (task counter, grid barrier, generation), one-CTA-per-SM persistent launch idiom. Depends on CUDA runtime only. |
15	| **Optimizer math** | `csrc/algorithms/<opt>.h` (×11) | Pure per-element apply math (`<opt>_step(...)`), no CUDA dependencies beyond `__device__` qualifiers, no state allocation, no I/O. Single source of truth — everything else `#include`s these (enforced by `scripts/check_math_single_source.py`). Already portable as-is. |
16	| **Optimizer tails** | `csrc/fused/sm_90/opt_components.cuh` | `apply_optimizer<OptId>(FusedOptState&, FusedScalars const&, ...)` — templates composing the algorithm headers into megakernel stages. Consumes the documented POD structs only. |
17	| **Model stages** | `csrc/fused/sm_90/model_stage_<model>.cuh` (decoder / vit / mamba3 — ONE HEADER PER MODEL, not a monolith) | Provides `model_<m>_forward_stage<Dims>` and `model_<m>_backward_stage<Dims>`: batch-slice-local fwd/bwd with all activations CTA-local, writing per-CTA weight-grad partials to a caller-provided workspace. Templated on compile-time dims (d_model, n_layers, n_heads, seq, vocab). Includes ONLY the substrate header + CUDA. No globals, no repo build flags (every `SG_TUNED_*` consumed via `#ifndef` defaults). |
18	| **Composition** | `csrc/fused/sm_90/fused_megakernel.cuh` | `launch_fused_megakernel<ModelId, OptId, Tier>` — stage pipeline: fwd → bwd → grid barrier → deterministic weight-grad reduction → optimizer tail. The only place stages and tails meet. |
19	| **Cells** | `csrc/fused/sm_90/mega_<model>_<opt>.cu` (×33) | GENERATED 36-line instantiations (`megakernel_codegen.py`). Never hand-edited. |
20	| **Dispatch** | `csrc/bindings/dispatch.cpp` + generated `fused_wired_cells.inc` / `fused_dispatch_table.inc` | `(model, optimizer, arch) → cell` routing. Generated from the same enumeration as the cells, so it cannot drift. Loud-gated: unwired/unready cells throw, never silently degrade. |
21	
22	## Portability rules (apply to every new/edited component)
23	1. **Self-containment**: a component header compiles with `#include <cuda_runtime.h>`
24	   + its declared includes only. Include-what-you-use; no transitive reliance.
25	2. **No hidden state**: no globals, no statics with side effects; all state flows
26	   through the documented POD structs (`PersistentContext`, `FusedOptState`,
27	   `FusedScalars`) or explicit pointers.
28	3. **Compile-time configuration only via documented template params or
29	   `#ifndef`-defaulted macros** (`SG_TUNED_*`); absent definitions must yield a
30	   correct (if untuned) kernel.
31	4. **The lift test**: copying `megakernel_common.cuh` + one `model_stage_*.cuh`
32	   + `opt_components.cuh` + the relevant `csrc/algorithms/*.h` into a fresh
33	   project and instantiating `launch_fused_megakernel<M,O,Tier>` must build and
34	   run. Each phase's validation includes compiling a minimal out-of-tree TU
35	   (tests/hw/test_component_portability.cu) that includes ONLY those headers.
36	5. **Generated artifacts are never edited by hand** — change the generator,
37	   regenerate everything, `git diff` must be generator-consistent.
38	6. **No placeholder math** on any wired path (owner no-suppression directive);
39	   surrogate stages exist only behind explicit unreadiness gates and throw at
40	   dispatch.
41	
42	## Phase status
43	- Phase 1 (in flight): real decoder fwd+bwd stages, validated vs eager — lands
44	  in `model_stages.cuh`, then is split per-model per this contract.
45	- Phase 2: vit + mamba3 stage headers (built against this contract natively).
46	- Phase 3: optimizer precompute stages in-kernel for the 9 non-trivial tails;
47	  SuperGrok2's CSA/HCA/PEER/GRU meta as in-kernel stages (the full
48	  "vit×sg2 in one binary").

1	# INTEGRATION-OPTSTAGES.md — wiring the in-kernel optimizer precompute stages
2	
3	**Scope.** This spec tells the binding/cell/codegen layer how to drive the
4	per-step PRECOMPUTE stages in `csrc/fused/sm_90/opt_stages_precompute.cuh` so
5	that every optimizer TAIL (`csrc/fused/sm_90/opt_components.cuh::apply_optimizer
6	<OptId>`) can run fully inside one persistent megakernel. It is a wiring
7	contract, not code: it does not touch `opt_components.cuh`,
8	`megakernel_codegen.py`, `dispatch.cpp`, `bindings.cpp`, or any
9	`supergrok2*`/`neuralgrok.py`/`grokadamw.py`/model-stage file (sibling-owned).
10	
11	Today only AdamW / Lion have a complete in-kernel tail (no precompute). The 9
12	non-trivial optimizers are classified below; the 4 STAGED ones get an upstream
13	stage that fills the `FusedOptState` fields their apply reads.
14	
15	---
16	
17	## 0. Verdict table (per-optimizer)
18	
19	| optimizer    | verdict        | what the apply reads | who produces it |
20	|--------------|----------------|----------------------|-----------------|
21	| grokfast     | NOTHING-NEEDED | (EMA fused in apply) | — `grokfast.h:63-65` |
22	| grokadamw    | NOTHING-NEEDED | (EMA fused in apply) | — `grokadamw.h:48-49` |
23	| neuralgrok   | NOTHING-NEEDED | (psi MLP inline)     | — `opt_components.cuh:222-229` → `neuralgrok.h:31-46` |
24	| looksam      | MODEL-COUPLED  | `st.sam_dir`         | **model stage** (2nd backward), `looksam.h:52-59` |
25	| prodigy      | STAGED         | `st.d_factor`        | `prodigy_precompute_*` |
26	| muon         | STAGED         | `st.orth`, `st.neg_lr_scale`, `st.decay_factor` | `muon_*` stage chain |
27	| supergrok11  | STAGED         | `st.mu`, `st.gate`   | `sg11_precompute_mu_and_gate_for_tensor` (per-tensor) |
28	| supergrok15  | STAGED         | `st.mu` (`st.gate` = host scalar) | `sg15_precompute_mu_for_tensor` (per-tensor) |
29	| supergrok2   | SKIP           | (sibling-owned)      | — |
30	
31	For the 3 NOTHING-NEEDED optimizers the codegen maps OptId → "no precompute
32	stage": their apply already runs a complete tail. `optimizer_needs_precompute
33	<Opt>::value` is `false` for them and a `static_assert` in
34	`optimizer_precompute_stage<Opt>` rejects an accidental instantiation.
35	
36	---
37	
38	## 1. The `PrecomputeWorkspace` POD (host allocation)
39	
40	The cross-CTA stages reduce through global scratch grouped in
41	`PrecomputeWorkspace` (mirrors `PersistentContext`: one POD so the codegen kernel
42	signature stays uniform). The host allocates ONLY the pointers the chosen
43	optimizer uses and zero-fills the rest; a stage dereferences only its own
44	optimizer's buffers. All FP32.
45	
46	| field | size (floats) | used by | meaning |
47	|-------|---------------|---------|---------|
48	| `prodigy_partials` | `2 * n_ctas` | prodigy | per-CTA (r,s) slots: `[0..n_ctas)`=r, `[n_ctas..2n_ctas)`=s |
49	| `prodigy_d` | `1` | prodigy | reduced d; bind `st.d_factor = prodigy_d[0]` |
50	| `muon_buf` | `rows*cols` | muon | momentum buffer (persists across steps) |
51	| `muon_X` | `rows*cols` | muon | current NS iterate |
52	| `muon_A` | `rows*rows` | muon | `A = X Xᵀ` |
53	| `muon_AX` | `rows*cols` | muon | `A X` |
54	| `muon_AAX` | `rows*cols` | muon | `A (A X)` |
55	| `muon_orth` | `rows*cols` | muon | NS output; bind `st.orth = muon_orth` |
56	| `muon_nrm_partials` | `n_ctas` | muon | per-CTA `‖buf‖_F²` slots |
57	| `muon_inv_norm` | `1` | muon | `1/(‖buf‖_F + 1e-7)` |
58	
59	`n_ctas == #SMs` (one persistent CTA per SM, `fused_megakernel.cuh:357`). The
60	muon matrix buffers are sized for the **largest** 2D weight processed (the stage
61	runs one matrix at a time; reuse the buffers across matrices).
62	
63	`prodigy_partials`, `muon_nrm_partials`, `prodigy_d`, `muon_inv_norm` must be
64	**zero-initialized before launch** (like the barrier counters,
65	`fused_megakernel.cuh:363-374`) — the owner-computes reducer reads every slot.
66	
67	---
68	
69	## 2. STAGED — prodigy (cross-ALL-tensors d, owner-computes tree)
70	
71	**Shape:** GLOBAL. One scalar `d` for the whole model; `r,s` sum over every
72	element of every parameter tensor.
73	
74	**Determinism deviation (contract-mandated, documented — not a transcription):**
75	the live per-op path reduces `r,s` with `atomicAdd` (`prodigy_sm90.cuh:105-108`,
76	`:135-138`). The COMPONENT_CONTRACT requires deterministic / no-float-atomic
77	reductions, so the stage REPLACES that with an owner-computes tree: each CTA
78	publishes its own `(r,s)` slot (no contention, no atomic) → grid barrier → one
79	owner thread sums the slots in ascending index order. Math-equivalent in exact
80	arithmetic; fp32 summation order is now fixed/reproducible.
81	
82	**Host/cell vs in-kernel split (faithful to the live multi-tensor driver):** the
83	PERSISTENT beta3-EMA decay of `(r,s)` across steps and the `d_coef` scaling live
84	in the host launcher (`prodigy_sm90.cuh:488-521`, `bindings.cpp:1246-1264`),
85	OUTSIDE `prodigy.h`. They are NOT in-kernel. The stage computes the INSTANTANEOUS
86	per-step `Σ r / Σ s` + `prodigy_update_d` (the cross-tensor reduction Audit-C
87	flagged). A cell that wants the grokking-race EMA estimator must, BETWEEN
88	phaseA-publish and phaseB-reduce: decay the prior `prodigy_partials` by `beta3`
89	and scale `r` by `d_coef` (host-side, on the workspace buffers) — exactly as the
90	live driver does around the same `prodigy_update_d`. The device math
91	(`prodigy.h`) stays byte-unchanged either way.
92	
93	**Codegen barrier sequence (per L3/L1 step):**
94	
95	```
96	// param_init = the Prodigy trajectory anchor (flat blob parallel to params).
97	optimizer_precompute_stage<Prodigy>(ctx, params, grad, sizes, offsets, st, ws,
98	                                    /*param_init=*/param_init);   // phaseA
99	bar.sync_reset(ctx.g_next_task);            // grid barrier; reset queue for reuse
100	prodigy_precompute_reduce_phaseB(ctx, st.d_factor, ws);          // owner-sum → d
101	bar.sync();                                  // d visible to all before apply
102	st.d_factor = ws.prodigy_d[0];               // bind the reduced d for the tail
103	// re-drain the queue for the apply (fused_optimizer_stage / the L3 bwd+opt):
104	apply_optimizer<Prodigy> over all tensors (opt_components.cuh:211-215).
105	```
106	
107	`st.d_factor` enters phaseA as `d_prev` (the comparison floor) and is OVERWRITTEN
108	post-reduce with the new `d`. Two grid barriers (reduce-publish, d-visible) plus
109	the queue resets — consistent with `fused_megakernel.cuh`'s phase pipeline.
110	
111	---
112	
113	## 3. STAGED — muon (Newton-Schulz orthogonalization, grid-cooperative)
114	
115	**Shape:** per-MATRIX, GRID-COOPERATIVE. A matmul is cross-element and a real 2D
116	weight does not fit one CTA's SMEM, so all CTAs cooperate on ONE matrix at a
117	time. This does NOT fit the flat one-CTA-per-tensor `(params, sizes, offsets)`
118	signature; the codegen drives the explicit phase fns (the
119	`optimizer_precompute_stage<Muon>` branch is a documented no-op that points
120	here).
121	
122	**New device code, cited:** the live path delegates `X Xᵀ`/`A X`/`A (A X)` to
123	`torch::mm`/cuBLAS (`bindings.cpp:992-994`), NOT a per-element canonical fn — so
124	the stage's tiled owner-computes matmul (`muon_matmul`) is legitimate new device
125	code, cited to that mm sequence. The drift guard requires only that the
126	ELEMENT-WISE pieces call `muon.h`: the momentum body and the NS polynomial
127	combine do (`muon_momentum_normalize_step` `muon.h:33-46`, `muon_ns_combine_step`
128	`muon.h:49-60`). The matmul contracts the k-dimension in ascending order (one
129	thread owns one output element) — deterministic fp32, no atomic.
130	
131	**1D params are NOT handled here** — they take the AdamW tail upstream
132	(`muon.h:75-76`, `bindings.cpp:970-977`). The codegen routes only 2D weights to
133	this stage.
134	
135	**Codegen sequence (per 2D matrix, `numel = rows*cols`, `ns_steps` default 5):**
136	
137	```
138	muon_momentum_norm_phaseA(grad_mtx, numel, momentum, ws);  // buf=μ·buf+g; ‖buf‖² slots
139	bar.sync();
140	muon_norm_reduce_phaseB(ctx, ws);                          // owner-sum → inv_norm
141	bar.sync();
142	muon_scale_X(numel, ws);                                   // X = buf*inv_norm (bindings.cpp:964)
143	bar.sync();
144	for (s = 0; s < ns_steps; ++s) {
145	    muon_matmul(ws.muon_X,  ws.muon_X, ws.muon_A,  rows, rows, cols, cols, cols, /*bT=*/true);  // A=XXᵀ
146	    bar.sync();
147	    muon_matmul(ws.muon_A,  ws.muon_X, ws.muon_AX, rows, cols, rows, rows, cols, /*bT=*/false); // AX
148	    bar.sync();
149	    muon_matmul(ws.muon_A,  ws.muon_AX,ws.muon_AAX,rows, cols, rows, rows, cols, /*bT=*/false); // A·AX
150	    bar.sync();
151	    muon_ns_combine_phase(numel, ws);                      // orth = a·X + b·AX + c·AAX
152	    bar.sync();
153	    std::swap(ws.muon_X, ws.muon_orth);  // next iter reads X; last iter result is in X
154	}
155	// After the loop the final orthogonalized matrix is in ws.muon_X (an odd # of
156	// swaps) — bind st.orth to whichever buffer holds the last combine output. With
157	// ns_steps swaps, the final result is in ws.muon_X iff ns_steps is even, else
158	// ws.muon_orth; the codegen tracks the parity (or copies into muon_orth once).
159	scale = 0.2f * sqrtf((float)max(rows, cols));   // bindings.cpp:981
160	st.orth         = <final NS buffer>;
161	st.neg_lr_scale = -lr * scale;                  // bindings.cpp:982
162	st.decay_factor = 1.0f - lr * wd;               // bindings.cpp:983
163	apply_optimizer<Muon> over this matrix (opt_components.cuh:230-234 → muon.h:63-73).
164	```
165	
166	`+1e-7` Frobenius-norm epsilon is in `muon_norm_reduce_phaseB`
167	(`opt_stages_precompute.cuh::kMuonNormEps`, `bindings.cpp:962`, `ref_muon_step`).
168	NS coefficients `(3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315)` are `kMuonNS_{A,B,C}`
169	(`bindings.cpp:938-940`).
170	
171	> Implementation note for the codegen author: per-matrix grid-cooperative
172	> orthogonalization inside ONE persistent megakernel is the heaviest stage; if a
173	> cell is register/SMEM-bound it may keep muon's NS as a SEPARATE launch (the L1
174	> tail still runs `apply_optimizer<Muon>` in-kernel reading `st.orth` produced by
175	> that launch) — exactly the split `opt_components.cuh:19-26` documents. The
176	> stage here makes the fully-in-kernel path POSSIBLE; choosing it per cell is a
177	> codegen/tier decision, not forced.
178	
179	---
180	
181	## 4. STAGED — supergrok11 (meta-MLP mu + per-TENSOR cosine gate)
182	
183	**Shape: PER-TENSOR, SINGLE-DRAIN, NO grid barrier** — and the "no barrier" is
184	correct for a SUBTLE reason, NOT by analogy to anything. The live per-op path
185	(`bindings.cpp:1407-1416`) loops per parameter doing metanet→gate→adam, with each
186	tensor SELF-CONTAINED: `gate(T)` and `apply(T)` depend ONLY on `mu(T)`, never on
187	any other tensor's mu (`bindings.cpp:1411` computes the gate INSIDE the per-param
188	loop; `compute_cosine_gate_fused` takes ONE tensor's smart_grad/mu). So mu/gate/
189	apply for one tensor fuse into ONE body owned end-to-end by the SAME CTA inside
190	the codegen's existing single task-queue drain (`fused_optimizer_stage`,
191	`fused_megakernel.cuh:101-142`).
192	
193	> **Why NOT a separate full-queue mu pre-pass (the rejected Design A):** a mu
194	> stage that drains the queue to `n_tasks` and a SEPARATE apply drain would (a)
195	> need a grid barrier for cross-CTA mu visibility AND (b) **silently no-op** — the
196	> apply drain's `next_block()` returns `t >= n_tasks` immediately (the counter was
197	> consumed) and never applies, unless a `sync_reset` re-zeros it. The single-drain
198	> per-tensor form has NO such hazard. (Prodigy DOES use a barrier because its `d`
199	> is a genuine cross-ALL-tensors reduction — SG11's gate is per-tensor, so the
200	> cases are NOT analogous.)
201	
202	- **mu(T) — per ELEMENT**: `mu[i] = rescale · phi(grad[i], sharpness[i])` over the
203	  tensor slice (the meta-net is a per-TENSOR weight set).
204	- **gate(T) — per TENSOR**: block-level cosine tree over the SAME tensor's
205	  elements via the deterministic `block_reduce_sum_f32` (`primitives.cuh:125`) —
206	  no cross-CTA, no atomic.
207	
208	`sg11_precompute_mu_and_gate_for_tensor<32>` does BOTH (mu→`__syncthreads`→gate)
209	in one per-tensor call and RETURNS the gate; `sg_stage_phi_weights<32>` stages the
210	phi weights to SMEM once per block before the loop.
211	
212	**Gate formula — mirror the CODE not the stale comment.**
213	`compute_cosine_gate_fused` (`supergrok11_sm90.cuh:280-285`) computes

94	## 2. THE one hard requirement: dynamic shared memory (don't drop it)
95	
96	Mamba's per-sample working set `MambaSampleSmem` is **145,124 bytes (≈141.72 KB)**
97	— **far over the 48 KB STATIC `__shared__` cap** (a static
98	`__shared__ MambaSampleSmem sm;` would **not compile**). This is an HONEST
99	deviation from the decoder's <48 KB static footprint: the decoder's
100	recompute-in-backward existed solely to clear 48 KB, but Mamba's **d_inner=256**
101	makes even one layer's activation set bump the cliff and the full live set is
102	~74 KB regardless — so recompute buys nothing, and the stages instead **cache both
103	layers' forward activations** (the clean, bug-free choice; the scan state stays in
104	per-thread registers, so smem does NOT explode to the ~128 KB an h-in-smem scan
105	would need).
106	
107	The composition launcher (`launch_fused_mamba_megakernel<Opt>`, to be written —
108	§3) MUST therefore declare the CTA smem **dynamic** and do **all three**:
109	
110	```cpp
111	const int dyn_smem = (int)sg::fused::sm90::kMambaSmemBytes;     // 145124
112	cudaFuncSetAttribute(&fused_mamba_megakernel<Opt>,
113	    cudaFuncAttributeMaxDynamicSharedMemorySize, dyn_smem);     // (1) opt-in >48KB
114	cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor(&occ, ..., dyn_smem); // (2) honest occ
115	fused_mamba_megakernel<Opt><<<grid, 256, dyn_smem, stream>>>(...);  // (3) launch
116	```
117	
118	and the kernel allocates the struct from dynamic smem:
119	`extern __shared__ char smem_raw[]; auto& sm = *reinterpret_cast<MambaSampleSmem*>(smem_raw);`
120	
121	**145124 B ≪ the sm_90 ~227 KB per-block dynamic-optin cap** (≈82 KB headroom;
122	`kMambaSmemBytes < 224*1024` is static_asserted in `mamba3_layout.cuh`), and the
123	persistent megakernel is **one-CTA-per-SM by design** (gridDim = #SMs, grid
124	barrier over #SMs), so **occupancy = 1 IS the design point** — a 142 KB block at
125	occ=1 is intended, not a regression. **Missing any of the three steps makes the
126	kernel silently fail to launch.** The launcher's only job beyond the decoder's is
127	to pass `dyn_smem` (NOT 0) in all three places, on a device whose
128	`MaxDynamicSharedMemoryPerBlockOptin ≥ 145124` (every sm_90 satisfies this; the
129	launcher should `assert(occ>=1)` and REFUSE — return
130	`cudaErrorLaunchOutOfResources` — rather than hang the grid barrier, exactly like
131	`launch_fused_decoder_megakernel`).

135	## 3. Composition + stage / barrier layout (one persistent kernel)
136	
137	`fused_mamba_megakernel.cuh` (to be written, modeled BYTE-FOR-BYTE on
138	`fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh` with the dynamic-smem changes from §2 and the
139	Mamba constants). gridDim = #SMs (one CTA/SM), 256 threads/CTA, **batch-parallel**
140	(NOT the param-tensor work-steal queue — that would vary the batch→CTA grouping
141	and fp32 sums aren't associative):
142	
143	```
144	P0  each CTA zeroes its OWN grad-partial slice + loss slot
145	--- grid barrier B0 ---
146	P1  each CTA owns a FIXED contiguous batch slice (blockIdx.x); processes its
147	    samples ONE AT A TIME (CTA-cooperative): broadcasts the sample's 8 int tokens
148	    + target into smem, runs mb_forward_sample + mb_backward_sample, accumulating
149	    each sample's weight-grad into the CTA's partial with a SINGLE-OWNER-THREAD-
150	    PER-ELEMENT rule (no atomics → deterministic), and sums its slice's NLL (fp32)
151	--- grid barrier B1 ---
152	P2  deterministic cross-CTA reduce: sum partial[0..nCTA) in ASCENDING CTA index
153	    into the global grad (no float atomics; order fixed → reuses the work-steal
154	    queue to pick WHO reduces which tensor). Loss: fp64 ordered sum → loss/B → a
155	    device float the host reads back.
156	--- grid barrier B2 (sync_reset: also resets the queue for P3) ---
157	P3  the REAL apply_optimizer<Opt> tail consumes the reduced grad in place
158	```

160	`n_tasks = 28` (`kMambaNumTensors`) for the reduce + optimizer phases; the kernel
161	reads per-tensor numel/offset from the generated `__constant__` tables
162	`kMambaSizes/kMambaOffsets` (mamba3_layout.cuh). Determinism: fixed batch→CTA
163	grouping + fixed ascending-CTA reduction order; **no float atomics** in the
164	weight-grad reduce.

191	The pybind `m.def("fused_step", ...)` arity is pinned in `bindings.cpp` (NOT
192	owned), so `fused_step`'s arity is unchanged. Carry the Mamba input through the
193	EXISTING `input`/`state`/`grad` tensors and add the **behavior** in `dispatch.cpp`
194	(owned), **identically to the decoder** (Mamba's input is int tokens, like the
195	decoder — NOT ViT's float pack).
196	
197	**Tensor contract (what Python passes; what dispatch.cpp reads):**
198	
199	* `input` = **int32** `[B*(8+1)]` contiguous — tokens `[B*8]` (row-major `[B][8]`)
200	  then targets `[B]`. `B = input.numel() / (kSeq+1) = numel / 9`. dispatch.cpp

87	// Sample-tile rows a CTA owns. Must be a multiple of 64 (wgmma atom M) AND of
88	// kSeq=8 (so a tile boundary is a sample boundary). kTileM=64 → 8 samples → one
89	// m64 atom (kAtomsM=1) — simpler than the decoder's stacked atoms.
90	constexpr int kTileM = SG_TUNED_TILE_M;
91	static_assert(kTileM % wgs::kWgmmaAtomM == 0,
92	              "SG_TUNED_TILE_M must be a multiple of 64 (wgmma m64 atom)");
93	static_assert(kTileM % mb::kSeq == 0,
94	              "SG_TUNED_TILE_M must be a multiple of kSeq=8 (tile=sample boundary)");
95	constexpr int kAtomsM = kTileM / wgs::kWgmmaAtomM;
96	constexpr int kSamplesPerTile = kTileM / mb::kSeq;

98	// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
99	//  Canonical Major-K smem stager (identical to the decoder TC's; the decoder
100	//  header is sibling-owned and off-limits to include, so the validated helper
101	//  is restated here — same INTERLEAVE layout the wgmma.cuh make_desc assumes:
102	//      idx(mn,k) = (k/8)*(MN*8) + mn*8 + (k%8)
103	//  Routes the source axis through an accessor so the SAME TransA=0/TransB=0
104	//  issue serves fwd / dX / dW; the staging loop transposes physically. ──────
105	template <int MN, typename Src>
106	__device__ __forceinline__ void stage_kmajor_tile(
107	        __nv_bfloat16* smem_tile, int kbase, Src src, int t0, int nthreads) {
108	    #pragma unroll 1
109	    for (int i = t0; i < MN * wgs::kWgmmaAtomK; i += nthreads) {
110	        const int mn = i / wgs::kWgmmaAtomK;
111	        const int k  = i % wgs::kWgmmaAtomK;
112	        const int dst = (k >> 3) * (MN * 8) + mn * 8 + (k & 7);
113	        smem_tile[dst] = src(mn, kbase + k);
114	    }
115	}

117	// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
118	//  Unpipelined single-CTA batch GEMM: D[M,N] = Σ_k A[m,k]·B[n,k], bf16 operands
119	//  (accessor-sourced + Major-K staged), fp32 accumulator, ascending-k. One
120	//  warpgroup (threads 0..127) issues the wgmma; all `nthreads` stage. Restated
121	//  from the decoder TC's tc_gemm_block_unpipelined (validated 13/13). MaxAtomsM
122	//  bounds the register accumulator (compile-time); m_atoms<=MaxAtomsM issue.
123	//  n_real<=N suppresses ragged pad columns. Determinism: ascending-k, one CTA.
124	// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
125	template <int N, int MaxAtomsM, typename SrcA, typename SrcB, typename Out>
126	__device__ void tc_gemm_block_unpipelined(
127	        int mbase0, int m_atoms, int n_real, int k_steps,
128	        SrcA srcA, SrcB srcB, Out out,
129	        __nv_bfloat16* smemA, __nv_bfloat16* smemB) {
130	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 900)
131	    const int tid = threadIdx.x;
132	    const int nthreads = blockDim.x;
133	    const bool in_wg0 = (tid < 128);
134	    const int tid_wg = tid & 127;
135	
136	    wgs::WgmmaAccum<N> acc[MaxAtomsM];
137	
138	    #pragma unroll 1
139	    for (int a = 0; a < m_atoms; ++a) {
140	        const int mbase = mbase0 + a * wgs::kWgmmaAtomM;
141	        if (in_wg0) wgs::wgmma_fence();
142	        #pragma unroll 1
143	        for (int k = 0; k < k_steps; ++k) {
144	            stage_kmajor_tile<wgs::kWgmmaAtomM>(
145	                smemA, k * wgs::kWgmmaAtomK,
146	                [&] (int mn, int kk) { return srcA(mbase + mn, kk); },
147	                tid, nthreads);
148	            stage_kmajor_tile<N>(
149	                smemB, k * wgs::kWgmmaAtomK,
150	                [&] (int mn, int kk) { return srcB(mn, kk); },
151	                tid, nthreads);
152	            __syncthreads();
153	            if (in_wg0) {
154	                wgs::SmemDesc dA = wgs::make_desc_A_kmajor<wgs::kWgmmaAtomM, wgs::kSwizzleNone>(smemA);
155	                wgs::SmemDesc dB = wgs::make_desc_B_kmajor<N, wgs::kSwizzleNone>(smemB);
156	                if (k == 0)
157	                    wgs::wgmma_m64nNk16_bf16<N, /*ScaleD=*/0, 0, 0>(acc[a], dA, dB);
158	                else
159	                    wgs::wgmma_m64nNk16_bf16<N, /*ScaleD=*/1, 0, 0>(acc[a], dA, dB);
160	                wgs::wgmma_commit_group();
161	                wgs::wgmma_wait_group<0>();
162	            }
163	            __syncthreads();
164	        }
165	        if (in_wg0) {
166	            #pragma unroll
167	            for (int i = 0; i < wgs::WgmmaAccum<N>::kRegs; ++i) {
168	                int row, col;
169	                wgs::wgmma_frag_decode(tid_wg, i, N, row, col);
170	                if (col < n_real) out(mbase + row, col, acc[a].c[i]);
171	            }
172	        }
173	        __syncthreads();
174	    }
175	#else
176	    (void)mbase0; (void)m_atoms; (void)n_real; (void)k_steps;
177	    (void)srcA; (void)srcB; (void)out; (void)smemA; (void)smemB;
178	#endif
179	}

181	// k_steps with PADDING: K is padded UP to a multiple of 16; the staging
182	// accessor must return 0 for k >= K_real (the pad rows). dt_proj contracts K=8,
183	// x_proj-dX contracts K=dbc=40 — NEITHER a multiple of 16. ceil, not floor.
184	__device__ __host__ __forceinline__ int kceil16(int K) {
185	    return (K + wgs::kWgmmaAtomK - 1) / wgs::kWgmmaAtomK;
186	}

188	// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
189	//  THIN ORIENTATION WRAPPERS (mbtc_gemm_*). Three accessor patterns: fwd
190	//  (Y=X·Wᵀ), dX (dX=dY·W, W transposed-staged), dW (dW=dYᵀ·X, both transposed,
191	//  K=T). M = kTileM (kAtomsM stacked atoms). Weights convert fp32→bf16 ON READ
192	//  (deterministic; no bf16 weight buffer). PAD-AWARE: srcA/srcB return 0 for
193	//  k >= K_real so a K not divisible by 16 (dt_proj K=8, x_proj-dX K=40) is
194	//  zero-extended; n_real marks the valid output columns for a ragged N tile.
195	// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
196	
197	// (fwd) Y[M,Nout] = X[M,Kin] @ W[Nout,Kin]ᵀ.  Tiles N over [0,Nout) in width-N
198	// atoms. Kin may be non-/16 (dt_proj Kin=dt_rank=8 → padded). Writes bf16
199	// Y [M,Nout] at `Yout` (the projection output, stored bf16).
200	template <int N>
201	__device__ __forceinline__ void mbtc_gemm_fwd_bf16(
202	        const __nv_bfloat16* __restrict__ X, const float* __restrict__ W,
203	        __nv_bfloat16* __restrict__ Yout, int Kin, int Nout,
204	        __nv_bfloat16* sA, __nv_bfloat16* sB) {
205	    const int k_steps = kceil16(Kin);
206	    for (int n0 = 0; n0 < Nout; n0 += N) {
207	        const int n_real = (Nout - n0) < N ? (Nout - n0) : N;
208	        auto srcA = [&] (int m, int k) -> __nv_bfloat16 {
209	            return k < Kin ? X[(int64_t)m * Kin + k] : __float2bfloat16(0.f); };
210	        auto srcB = [&] (int n, int k) -> __nv_bfloat16 {
211	            int nn = n0 + n; return (nn < Nout && k < Kin) ? __float2bfloat16(W[(int64_t)nn * Kin + k]) : __float2bfloat16(0.f); };
212	        auto out  = [&] (int m, int n, float v) {
213	            Yout[(int64_t)m * Nout + n0 + n] = __float2bfloat16(v); };
214	        tc_gemm_block_unpipelined<N, /*MaxAtomsM=*/kAtomsM>(
215	            0, kAtomsM, n_real, k_steps, srcA, srcB, out, sA, sB);
216	    }
217	}

220	// outputs consumed by fp32 elementwise stages (dt_pre, the scan inputs).
221	template <int N>
222	__device__ __forceinline__ void mbtc_gemm_fwd_f32(
223	        const __nv_bfloat16* __restrict__ X, const float* __restrict__ W,
224	        float* __restrict__ Yf32, int Kin, int Nout,
225	        __nv_bfloat16* sA, __nv_bfloat16* sB) {
226	    const int k_steps = kceil16(Kin);
227	    for (int n0 = 0; n0 < Nout; n0 += N) {
228	        const int n_real = (Nout - n0) < N ? (Nout - n0) : N;
229	        auto srcA = [&] (int m, int k) -> __nv_bfloat16 {
230	            return k < Kin ? X[(int64_t)m * Kin + k] : __float2bfloat16(0.f); };
231	        auto srcB = [&] (int n, int k) -> __nv_bfloat16 {
232	            int nn = n0 + n; return (nn < Nout && k < Kin) ? __float2bfloat16(W[(int64_t)nn * Kin + k]) : __float2bfloat16(0.f); };
233	        auto out  = [&] (int m, int n, float v) { Yf32[(int64_t)m * Nout + n0 + n] = v; };
234	        tc_gemm_block_unpipelined<N, /*MaxAtomsM=*/kAtomsM>(
235	            0, kAtomsM, n_real, k_steps, srcA, srcB, out, sA, sB);

239	// (dX) dX[M,Kin] = dY[M,Nout] @ W[Nout,Kin].  N(wgmma)=Kin (tiled by N). K=Nout
240	// (the contracted out_dim) — may be non-/16 (x_proj dX K=dbc=40 → padded).
241	// W staged transposed: srcB(n=kin, k=out)=W[out·Kin+kin]. Writes fp32 dX [M,Kin].
242	template <int N>
243	__device__ __forceinline__ void mbtc_gemm_dx_f32(
244	        const __nv_bfloat16* __restrict__ dY, const float* __restrict__ W,
245	        float* __restrict__ dXf32, int Kin, int Nout,
246	        __nv_bfloat16* sA, __nv_bfloat16* sB) {
247	    const int k_steps = kceil16(Nout);
248	    for (int n0 = 0; n0 < Kin; n0 += N) {
249	        const int n_real = (Kin - n0) < N ? (Kin - n0) : N;
250	        auto srcA = [&] (int m, int k) -> __nv_bfloat16 {
251	            return k < Nout ? dY[(int64_t)m * Nout + k] : __float2bfloat16(0.f); };
252	        auto srcB = [&] (int n, int k) -> __nv_bfloat16 {
253	            int nn = n0 + n; return (nn < Kin && k < Nout) ? __float2bfloat16(W[(int64_t)k * Kin + nn]) : __float2bfloat16(0.f); };
254	        auto out  = [&] (int m, int n, float v) { dXf32[(int64_t)m * Kin + n0 + n] = v; };
255	        tc_gemm_block_unpipelined<N, /*MaxAtomsM=*/kAtomsM>(
256	            0, kAtomsM, n_real, k_steps, srcA, srcB, out, sA, sB);
257	    }
258	}

260	// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
261	//  HBM bf16 ACTS buffer (Fork B). The projection-dW operands (X-inputs and
262	//  dY-adjoints) the cross-tile P2 dW owners read. Token-row-major [T, width]
263	//  (= sample-major [nsamp][kSeq][width] since rows are sample-ordered). Carved
264	//  from the FRONT of the workspace; offsets are RUNTIME (depend on T=B·kSeq).
265	//
266	//  The 4 projections' dW = dYᵀ@X needs, per layer:
267	//    in_proj  dW[512,128] = dxz^T  @ layer_in : X_in    [T,128], dY_dxz   [T,512]
268	//    x_proj   dW[40,256]  = dxdbc^T@ x_main   : X_xmain  [T,256], dY_dxdbc [T,40]
269	//    dt_proj  dW[256,8]   = ddtpre^T@ dt_raw  : X_dtraw  [T,8],   dY_ddtpre[T,256]
270	//    out_proj dW[128,256] = dyout^T @ y_gated : X_ygated [T,256], dY_dyout [T,128]
271	//  (dt_proj.bias = Σ_T ddt_pre — free P2 bias pass. in/x/out_proj have no bias.)
272	//  The HEAD (out.w/out.b) stays scalar → no acts. dh0 [T,128] feeds tok/pos owner-scan.
273	// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
274	// (still in namespace mbtc — opened above)
275	
276	struct MbActs {
277	    __nv_bfloat16* X_in[mb::kLayers];      // [T, d]        in_proj input (layer input, bf16)
278	    __nv_bfloat16* X_xmain[mb::kLayers];   // [T, d_inner]  x_proj input (bf16 copy of x_main)
279	    __nv_bfloat16* X_dtraw[mb::kLayers];   // [T, dt_rank]  dt_proj input (bf16 dt_raw)
280	    __nv_bfloat16* X_ygated[mb::kLayers];  // [T, d_inner]  out_proj input (bf16 y_gated)
281	    __nv_bfloat16* dY_dxz[mb::kLayers];    // [T, 2*d_inner] in_proj output adjoint (bf16 dxz)
282	    __nv_bfloat16* dY_dxdbc[mb::kLayers];  // [T, dbc]      x_proj output adjoint (bf16 dx_dbc)
283	    __nv_bfloat16* dY_ddtpre[mb::kLayers]; // [T, d_inner]  dt_proj output adjoint (bf16 ddt_pre)
284	    __nv_bfloat16* dY_dyout[mb::kLayers];  // [T, d]        out_proj output adjoint (bf16 dy_out)
285	    __nv_bfloat16* dh0;                    // [T, d]        embedding-input adjoint
286	};
287	
288	// Running bf16-element offset for the acts region (host + device must agree).
289	__host__ __device__ __forceinline__ int64_t mb_acts_bf16_count(int T) {
290	    const int64_t d = mb::kD, di = mb::kDInner, dr = mb::kDtRank, dbc = mb::kDbc;
291	    const int64_t Td = (int64_t)T * d, Tdi = (int64_t)T * di, Tdr = (int64_t)T * dr,
292	                  Tdbc = (int64_t)T * dbc, T2di = (int64_t)T * 2 * di;
293	    int64_t bf = 0;
294	    for (int li = 0; li < mb::kLayers; ++li)
295	        bf += Td + Tdi + Tdr + Tdi + T2di + Tdbc + Tdi + Td;   // X_in,X_xmain,X_dtraw,X_ygated,dY_dxz,dY_dxdbc,dY_ddtpre,dY_dyout
296	    bf += Td;                                                  // dh0
297	    return bf;
298	}
299	__host__ __device__ __forceinline__ int64_t mb_acts_floats(int T) {
300	    return (mb_acts_bf16_count(T) + 1) / 2;
301	}
302	
303	__device__ __forceinline__ MbActs mb_acts_bind(__nv_bfloat16* p, int T) {
304	    MbActs a;
305	    int64_t off = 0;
306	    const int64_t Td = (int64_t)T * mb::kD, Tdi = (int64_t)T * mb::kDInner,
307	                  Tdr = (int64_t)T * mb::kDtRank, Tdbc = (int64_t)T * mb::kDbc,
308	                  T2di = (int64_t)T * 2 * mb::kDInner;
309	    for (int li = 0; li < mb::kLayers; ++li) {
310	        a.X_in[li]      = p + off; off += Td;
311	        a.X_xmain[li]   = p + off; off += Tdi;
312	        a.X_dtraw[li]   = p + off; off += Tdr;
313	        a.X_ygated[li]  = p + off; off += Tdi;
314	        a.dY_dxz[li]    = p + off; off += T2di;
315	        a.dY_dxdbc[li]  = p + off; off += Tdbc;
316	        a.dY_ddtpre[li] = p + off; off += Tdi;
317	        a.dY_dyout[li]  = p + off; off += Td;
318	    }
319	    a.dh0 = p + off; off += Td;
320	    return a;
321	}

323	// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
324	//  Per-CTA TILE SCRATCH (HBM). The fwd-all-layers-then-bwd-all-layers order
325	//  (the decoder's line-377 lesson) means every sample's forward activations the
326	//  backward reads must be cached PER (layer, sample) — so `act` is typed as the
327	//  REAL scalar MambaSampleSmem::LayerAct, [kLayers][nsamp], letting the scalar
328	//  mb_scan_fwd/bwd be called VERBATIM with `a = &act[li][si]` (they deref only
329	//  a->dt_pre/Bmat/Cmat; no __shared__ assumption — so the cache is HBM, the
330	//  launcher stays STATIC-smem, no dynamic opt-in). Plus the residual chain
331	//  (layer_in / final_in) and the transient fp32 buffers the per-tile fwd/bwd use.
332	//  One slab per CTA (a CTA finishes a tile fwd+bwd before the next).
333	//
334	//  All per-sample scalar calls (scan/conv/LN) take a CONTIGUOUS [kSeq,width]
335	//  one-sample slice: `buf + si*kSeq*width`. Since rows are sample-major
336	//  (row m = si*kSeq + t), a token-row-major [T_tile,width] buffer IS that
337	//  sample-major slice — the TC projection's out(m,·) and the scalar fn's
338	//  [kSeq,width] view coincide with NO reshape.
339	// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
340	struct MbTileScratch {
341	    MambaSampleSmem::LayerAct* act[mb::kLayers];  // [nsamp] each — the bwd cache
342	    float* layer_in[mb::kLayers];   // [kTileM, d]      residual / layer input (fp32)
343	    float* final_in;                // [kTileM, d]      last-layer output (fp32, head input)
344	    // transient fp32 tile buffers (reused within a tile):
345	    float* xmain;                   // [kTileM, d_inner] silu(conv) (fp32, scan input + D-skip)
346	    float* work_di;                 // [kTileM, d_inner] general d_inner-wide fp32 scratch
347	    float* work_di2;                // [kTileM, d_inner] second d_inner-wide scratch
348	    float* work_d;                  // [kTileM, d]       d-wide fp32 scratch (LN in/out, residual)
349	    float* dbc;                     // [kTileM, dbc]     x_dbc / dx_dbc staging (fp32)
350	    float* fn_xhat;                 // [kTileM, d]       final-norm xhat cache (last pos used)
351	    float* fn_inv;                  // [kTileM]          final-norm inv cache
352	    float* logits;                  // [nsamp, kPHead]   per-sample last-pos logits (fp32)
353	};
354	
355	constexpr int kNSampPerTile = kTileM / mb::kSeq;
356	constexpr int kLayerActFloats = (int)(sizeof(MambaSampleSmem::LayerAct) / sizeof(float));
357	
358	__host__ __device__ __forceinline__ int64_t mb_tile_scratch_floats() {
359	    const int64_t TMd = (int64_t)kTileM * mb::kD, TMdi = (int64_t)kTileM * mb::kDInner,
360	                  TMdbc = (int64_t)kTileM * mb::kDbc;
361	    int64_t f = 0;
362	    f += (int64_t)mb::kLayers * kNSampPerTile * kLayerActFloats;   // act[L][nsamp]
363	    f += (int64_t)mb::kLayers * TMd;                               // layer_in[L]
364	    f += TMd;                                                      // final_in
365	    f += TMdi + TMdi + TMdi + TMd + TMdbc;                         // xmain,work_di,work_di2,work_d,dbc
366	    f += TMd + kTileM;                                             // fn_xhat,fn_inv
367	    f += (int64_t)kNSampPerTile * mb::kPHead;                      // logits
368	    return f;
369	}
370	
371	__device__ __forceinline__ MbTileScratch mb_tile_scratch_bind(float* slab) {
372	    MbTileScratch s;
373	    int64_t o = 0;
374	    for (int li = 0; li < mb::kLayers; ++li) {
375	        s.act[li] = reinterpret_cast<MambaSampleSmem::LayerAct*>(slab + o);
376	        o += (int64_t)kNSampPerTile * kLayerActFloats;
377	    }
378	    for (int li = 0; li < mb::kLayers; ++li) { s.layer_in[li] = slab + o; o += (int64_t)kTileM * mb::kD; }
379	    s.final_in = slab + o; o += (int64_t)kTileM * mb::kD;
380	    s.xmain    = slab + o; o += (int64_t)kTileM * mb::kDInner;
381	    s.work_di  = slab + o; o += (int64_t)kTileM * mb::kDInner;
382	    s.work_di2 = slab + o; o += (int64_t)kTileM * mb::kDInner;
383	    s.work_d   = slab + o; o += (int64_t)kTileM * mb::kD;
384	    s.dbc      = slab + o; o += (int64_t)kTileM * mb::kDbc;
385	    s.fn_xhat  = slab + o; o += (int64_t)kTileM * mb::kD;
386	    s.fn_inv   = slab + o; o += kTileM;
387	    s.logits   = slab + o; o += (int64_t)kNSampPerTile * mb::kPHead;
388	    return s;
389	}
