391	// ── LN-vector + scan/conv grad partials layout (the NON-GEMM grads Fork B keeps
392	//    tile-local, reduced ascending-CTA in P2). Per CTA, in this dense order:
393	//      [0]            A_log  [d_inner*state]   (per layer ×L)
394	//      ...            D      [d_inner]
395	//      ...            conv_w [d_inner*conv_k]
396	//      ...            conv_b [d_inner]
397	//      ...            n_w    [d]               (per-layer norm)
398	//      ...            n_b    [d]
399	//      (after L layers) head norm_w [d], norm_b [d], head out_w [pHead*d], out_b [pHead]
400	//    Each is summed across CTAs in P2. The per-layer block repeats L times; the
401	//    head block once. The dt_proj.bias is NOT here (it is the free GEMM bias).
402	// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
403	constexpr int kPartPerLayer =
404	      mb::kDInner * mb::kState   // A_log
405	    + mb::kDInner               // D
406	    + mb::kDInner * mb::kConvK  // conv_w
407	    + mb::kDInner               // conv_b
408	    + mb::kD                    // n_w
409	    + mb::kD;                   // n_b
410	constexpr int kPartHead =
411	      mb::kD + mb::kD                 // norm_w, norm_b
412	    + mb::kPHead * mb::kD + mb::kPHead; // out_w, out_b
413	constexpr int kPartElems = mb::kLayers * kPartPerLayer + kPartHead;
414	
415	// Typed view over ONE CTA's partial slab (so the P1 accumulators write by name).
416	struct MbPartial {
417	    float* A_log[mb::kLayers]; float* D[mb::kLayers];
418	    float* conv_w[mb::kLayers]; float* conv_b[mb::kLayers];
419	    float* n_w[mb::kLayers]; float* n_b[mb::kLayers];
420	    float* norm_w; float* norm_b; float* out_w; float* out_b;
421	};
422	__device__ __forceinline__ MbPartial mb_partial_bind(float* base) {
423	    MbPartial p; int64_t o = 0;
424	    for (int li = 0; li < mb::kLayers; ++li) {
425	        p.A_log[li]  = base + o; o += mb::kDInner * mb::kState;
426	        p.D[li]      = base + o; o += mb::kDInner;
427	        p.conv_w[li] = base + o; o += mb::kDInner * mb::kConvK;
428	        p.conv_b[li] = base + o; o += mb::kDInner;
429	        p.n_w[li]    = base + o; o += mb::kD;
430	        p.n_b[li]    = base + o; o += mb::kD;
431	    }
432	    p.norm_w = base + o; o += mb::kD;
433	    p.norm_b = base + o; o += mb::kD;
434	    p.out_w  = base + o; o += mb::kPHead * mb::kD;
435	    p.out_b  = base + o; o += mb::kPHead;
436	    return p;
437	}
438	// The dec_layout tensor index for each partial slot, in P2 reduce order. Built at
439	// runtime in the reduce (functions of li) — see mbtc_partial_reduce.
440	
441	// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
442	//  FORWARD over one SAMPLE TILE (nsamp = nrows/kSeq samples, kTileM rows), global
443	//  token rows [g0, g0+nrows). The 4 PROJECTIONS run tile-wide on wgmma (M=nrows);
444	//  conv1d / selective-scan / gate / skip / LN / head / CE run PER-SAMPLE scalar
445	//  (REUSING model_stage_mamba3.cuh's mb_conv1d_fwd / mb_scan_fwd / mb_layernorm_fwd
446	//  verbatim with a = &act[li][si]). Writes the MbActs projection operands (bf16)
447	//  + the per-(layer,sample) LayerAct caches the bwd reads; returns the tile's
448	//  summed NLL (thread 0 holds it). tok_ids/tgt_ids are HBM int32.
449	//
450	//  Mirrors mb_forward_sample's math EXACTLY; the precision fork: layer_in bf16
451	//  (in_proj + residual), x_main/dt_raw fp32 into scan/conv/gate with ONLY the
452	//  bf16 copy consumed by x_proj/dt_proj rounded; LN/scan/conv/gate/head fp32.
453	// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
454	__device__ float mbtc_forward_tile(
455	        const MambaWeights& w, int g0, int nrows, const MbActs& acts,
456	        const MbTileScratch& sc, const int* __restrict__ tok_ids,
457	        const int* __restrict__ tgt_ids,
458	        __nv_bfloat16* sA, __nv_bfloat16* sB, float* red) {
459	    const int nsamp = nrows / mb::kSeq;
460	    // ── Embedding: X_in[0][g] = tok[id] + pos[s%S]. bf16. ──
461	    for (int idx = threadIdx.x; idx < nrows * mb::kD; idx += blockDim.x) {
462	        const int r = idx / mb::kD, j = idx % mb::kD;
463	        const int g = g0 + r;
464	        const int tid = tok_ids[g];
465	        const int sp = g % mb::kSeq;
466	        float v = w.tok[(int64_t)tid * mb::kD + j] + w.pos[(int64_t)sp * mb::kD + j];
467	        acts.X_in[0][(int64_t)g * mb::kD + j] = __float2bfloat16(v);
468	    }
469	    __syncthreads();
470	
471	    for (int li = 0; li < mb::kLayers; ++li) {
472	        const MambaWeights::Layer& L = w.layer[li];
473	        const __nv_bfloat16* Xin = acts.X_in[li] + (int64_t)g0 * mb::kD;   // [nrows,d] bf16
474	        // (a) in_proj (TC): xz = Xin @ in_w^T (N=2*d_inner, K=d). Route split → the
475	        //     LayerAct caches act[li][si].x_main_raw / .z (fp32, the scan/conv inputs).
476	        {
477	            auto srcA = [&] (int m, int k) -> __nv_bfloat16 { return Xin[(int64_t)m * mb::kD + k]; };
478	            for (int n0 = 0; n0 < 2 * mb::kDInner; n0 += SG_TUNED_TILE_N) {
479	                const int N = SG_TUNED_TILE_N;
480	                const int n_real = (2 * mb::kDInner - n0) < N ? (2 * mb::kDInner - n0) : N;
481	                auto srcB = [&] (int n, int k) -> __nv_bfloat16 {
482	                    int nn = n0 + n; return nn < 2 * mb::kDInner ? __float2bfloat16(L.in_w[(int64_t)nn * mb::kD + k]) : __float2bfloat16(0.f); };
483	                auto out = [&] (int m, int n, float v) {
484	                    const int si = m / mb::kSeq, t = m % mb::kSeq; const int o = n0 + n;
485	                    if (o < mb::kDInner) sc.act[li][si].x_main_raw[t][o] = v;
486	                    else sc.act[li][si].z[t][o - mb::kDInner] = v; };
487	                tc_gemm_block_unpipelined<SG_TUNED_TILE_N, /*MaxAtomsM=*/kAtomsM>(
488	                    0, kAtomsM, n_real, kceil16(mb::kD), srcA, srcB, out, sA, sB);
489	            }
490	        }
491	        __syncthreads();
492	        // (b) conv1d (scalar, per-sample) → act.conv (PRE-silu cache); x_main =
493	        //     silu(conv) → sc.xmain tile buffer (fp32) AND bf16 → X_xmain (x_proj dW operand).
494	        for (int si = 0; si < nsamp; ++si) {
495	            MambaSampleSmem::LayerAct* a = &sc.act[li][si];
496	            mb_conv1d_fwd(&a->x_main_raw[0][0], L.conv_w, L.conv_b, &a->conv[0][0]);
497	        }
498	        for (int idx = threadIdx.x; idx < nrows * mb::kDInner; idx += blockDim.x) {
499	            const int si = idx / (mb::kSeq * mb::kDInner);
500	            const int rem = idx % (mb::kSeq * mb::kDInner);
501	            const int t = rem / mb::kDInner, c = rem % mb::kDInner;
502	            float xm = mb_silu(sc.act[li][si].conv[t][c]);
503	            sc.xmain[(int64_t)(si * mb::kSeq + t) * mb::kDInner + c] = xm;
504	            acts.X_xmain[li][(int64_t)(g0 + si * mb::kSeq + t) * mb::kDInner + c] = __float2bfloat16(xm);
505	        }
506	        __syncthreads();
507	        // (c) x_proj (TC): x_dbc = x_main(bf16) @ x_proj_w^T (N=dbc=40, K=d_inner).
508	        //     fp32 → sc.dbc; split → dt_raw[:, :8] (→ bf16 X_dtraw + kept in dbc),
509	        //     Bmat/Cmat → act caches.
510	        mbtc_gemm_fwd_f32<SG_TUNED_TILE_N>(acts.X_xmain[li] + (int64_t)g0 * mb::kDInner, L.x_proj_w,
511	                                           sc.dbc, mb::kDInner, mb::kDbc, sA, sB);
512	        __syncthreads();
513	        for (int idx = threadIdx.x; idx < nrows * mb::kDbc; idx += blockDim.x) {
514	            const int r = idx / mb::kDbc, o = idx % mb::kDbc;
515	            const int si = r / mb::kSeq, t = r % mb::kSeq;
516	            float v = sc.dbc[(int64_t)r * mb::kDbc + o];
517	            if (o < mb::kDtRank)
518	                acts.X_dtraw[li][(int64_t)(g0 + r) * mb::kDtRank + o] = __float2bfloat16(v);  // dt_raw bf16 (dt_proj dW operand)
519	            else if (o < mb::kDtRank + mb::kState) sc.act[li][si].Bmat[t][o - mb::kDtRank] = v;
520	            else sc.act[li][si].Cmat[t][o - mb::kDtRank - mb::kState] = v;
521	        }
522	        __syncthreads();
523	        // (d) dt_proj (TC): dt_pre = dt_raw(bf16) @ dt_proj_w^T + bias (N=d_inner,
524	        //     K=dt_rank=8 PADDED→16). Bias added in the scalar epilogue. fp32 →
525	        //     act.dt_pre. The GEMM emits WITHOUT bias; add it on read-back.
526	        mbtc_gemm_fwd_f32<SG_TUNED_TILE_N>(acts.X_dtraw[li] + (int64_t)g0 * mb::kDtRank, L.dt_proj_w,
527	                                           sc.work_di, mb::kDtRank, mb::kDInner, sA, sB);
528	        __syncthreads();
529	        for (int idx = threadIdx.x; idx < nrows * mb::kDInner; idx += blockDim.x) {
530	            const int si = idx / (mb::kSeq * mb::kDInner);
531	            const int rem = idx % (mb::kSeq * mb::kDInner);
532	            const int t = rem / mb::kDInner, o = rem % mb::kDInner;
533	            sc.act[li][si].dt_pre[t][o] = sc.work_di[(int64_t)(si * mb::kSeq + t) * mb::kDInner + o] + L.dt_proj_b[o];
534	        }
535	        __syncthreads();
536	        // (e) selective scan (scalar, per-sample) → act.y_scan. x_main one-sample
537	        //     slice = sc.xmain + si*kSeq*d_inner (contiguous [kSeq,d_inner]).
538	        for (int si = 0; si < nsamp; ++si) {
539	            MambaSampleSmem::LayerAct* a = &sc.act[li][si];
540	            mb_scan_fwd(L.A_log, sc.xmain + (int64_t)si * mb::kSeq * mb::kDInner, a, &a->y_scan[0][0]);
541	        }
542	        // (f) gate+skip: y_gated = (y_scan + x_main*D)*silu(z) → sc.work_di (fp32)
543	        //     AND bf16 → X_ygated (out_proj dW operand).
544	        for (int idx = threadIdx.x; idx < nrows * mb::kDInner; idx += blockDim.x) {
545	            const int si = idx / (mb::kSeq * mb::kDInner);
546	            const int rem = idx % (mb::kSeq * mb::kDInner);
547	            const int t = rem / mb::kDInner, c = rem % mb::kDInner;
548	            const int r = si * mb::kSeq + t;
549	            MambaSampleSmem::LayerAct* a = &sc.act[li][si];
550	            float yv = a->y_scan[t][c] + sc.xmain[(int64_t)r * mb::kDInner + c] * L.D[c];
551	            float yg = yv * mb_silu(a->z[t][c]);
552	            sc.work_di[(int64_t)r * mb::kDInner + c] = yg;
553	            acts.X_ygated[li][(int64_t)(g0 + r) * mb::kDInner + c] = __float2bfloat16(yg);
554	        }
555	        __syncthreads();
556	        // (g) out_proj (TC): y_out = y_gated(bf16) @ out_w^T (N=d, K=d_inner). fp32
557	        //     → sc.work_d; r = y_out + residual(Xin bf16→fp32) → sc.work_d.
558	        mbtc_gemm_fwd_f32<SG_TUNED_TILE_N>(acts.X_ygated[li] + (int64_t)g0 * mb::kDInner, L.out_w,
559	                                           sc.work_d, mb::kDInner, mb::kD, sA, sB);
560	        __syncthreads();
561	        for (int idx = threadIdx.x; idx < nrows * mb::kD; idx += blockDim.x) {
562	            const int r = idx / mb::kD, j = idx % mb::kD;
563	            sc.work_d[(int64_t)r * mb::kD + j] += __bfloat162float(Xin[(int64_t)r * mb::kD + j]);
564	        }
565	        __syncthreads();
566	        // (h) LN (scalar, per-sample) → next layer_in (bf16) / final_in (fp32) + act.ln caches.
567	        float* dst = (li + 1 < mb::kLayers) ? sc.layer_in[li + 1] : sc.final_in;
568	        for (int si = 0; si < nsamp; ++si) {
569	            MambaSampleSmem::LayerAct* a = &sc.act[li][si];
570	            const int r0 = si * mb::kSeq;
571	            mb_layernorm_fwd(sc.work_d + (int64_t)r0 * mb::kD, L.n_w, L.n_b,
572	                             dst + (int64_t)r0 * mb::kD, &a->ln_xhat[0][0], &a->ln_inv[0], red, mb::kD);
573	        }
574	        if (li + 1 < mb::kLayers) {
575	            for (int idx = threadIdx.x; idx < nrows * mb::kD; idx += blockDim.x) {
576	                const int r = idx / mb::kD, j = idx % mb::kD;
577	                acts.X_in[li + 1][(int64_t)(g0 + r) * mb::kD + j] = __float2bfloat16(sc.layer_in[li + 1][(int64_t)r * mb::kD + j]);
578	            }
579	            __syncthreads();
580	        }
581	    }
582	
583	    // ── Final norm + head + CE, scalar PER-SAMPLE on the LAST position only. ──
584	    float nll_acc = 0.0f;
585	    for (int si = 0; si < nsamp; ++si) {
586	        const int rlast = si * mb::kSeq + (mb::kSeq - 1);
587	        const float* hlast = sc.final_in + (int64_t)rlast * mb::kD;
588	        float sum = 0.0f;
589	        for (int j = threadIdx.x; j < mb::kD; j += blockDim.x) sum += hlast[j];
590	        float mean = mb_block_sum(sum, red) / (float)mb::kD;
591	        float vs = 0.0f;
592	        for (int j = threadIdx.x; j < mb::kD; j += blockDim.x) { float c = hlast[j] - mean; vs += c * c; }
593	        float var = mb_block_sum(vs, red) / (float)mb::kD;
594	        float iv = rsqrtf(var + mb::kLnEps);
595	        if (threadIdx.x == 0) sc.fn_inv[rlast] = iv;
596	        // hn = xhat*norm_w + norm_b → sc.work_d row rlast (head input, fp32, scalar head).
597	        for (int j = threadIdx.x; j < mb::kD; j += blockDim.x) {
598	            float xh = (hlast[j] - mean) * iv;
599	            sc.fn_xhat[(int64_t)rlast * mb::kD + j] = xh;
600	            sc.work_d[(int64_t)rlast * mb::kD + j] = xh * w.norm_w[j] + w.norm_b[j];
601	        }
602	        __syncthreads();
603	        // logits[o] = hn · out_w[o] + out_b[o] (scalar head, fp32). Store sc.logits[si].
604	        float* lg = sc.logits + (int64_t)si * mb::kPHead;
605	        const float* hn = sc.work_d + (int64_t)rlast * mb::kD;
606	        for (int o = threadIdx.x; o < mb::kPHead; o += blockDim.x) {
607	            const float* Wr = w.out_w + (int64_t)o * mb::kD;
608	            float acc = w.out_b[o];
609	            #pragma unroll 4
610	            for (int k = 0; k < mb::kD; ++k) acc += hn[k] * Wr[k];
611	            lg[o] = acc;
612	        }
613	        __syncthreads();
614	        int tgt = tgt_ids[g0 / mb::kSeq + si];
615	        float lmax = -CUDART_INF_F;
616	        for (int o = threadIdx.x; o < mb::kPHead; o += blockDim.x) lmax = fmaxf(lmax, lg[o]);
617	        lmax = mb_block_max(lmax, red);
618	        float es = 0.0f;
619	        for (int o = threadIdx.x; o < mb::kPHead; o += blockDim.x) es += __expf(lg[o] - lmax);
620	        es = mb_block_sum(es, red);
621	        float logz = lmax + __logf(es);
622	        if (threadIdx.x == 0) nll_acc += (logz - lg[tgt]);
623	        __syncthreads();
624	    }
625	    return nll_acc;
626	}
627	
628	// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
629	//  BACKWARD over one SAMPLE TILE. Assumes mbtc_forward_tile ran for THIS tile
630	//  (act caches + final/fn caches + logits populated). The 4 PROJECTIONS compute
631	//  dX via wgmma and WRITE the dY output-adjoints to MbActs (dY_dxz/dY_dxdbc/
632	//  dY_ddtpre/dY_dyout) + dh0 for P2's output-stationary dW (it does NOT touch the
633	//  proj dW here). The scan/conv (per-sample scalar, REUSED mb_scan_bwd /
634	//  mb_conv1d_bwd) + the gate/skip + LN + scalar head accumulate A_log/D/conv_w/b/
635	//  n_w/b/norm/out into the per-CTA partial `part`. `B` is the full batch (CE mean).
636	//  Mirrors mb_backward_sample's order 1..13 exactly.
637	//
638	//  smem: `dBmat_s`/`dCmat_s` [kSeq*kState] each (the scan-bwd cross-channel reduce
639	//  target, zeroed + consumed PER SAMPLE). `red` the reduction slot.
640	// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
641	__device__ void mbtc_backward_tile(
642	        const MambaWeights& w, int g0, int nrows, int B, const MbActs& acts,
643	        const MbTileScratch& sc, const MbPartial& part,
644	        const int* __restrict__ tok_ids, const int* __restrict__ tgt_ids,
645	        __nv_bfloat16* sA, __nv_bfloat16* sB, float* red,
646	        float* dBmat_s, float* dCmat_s) {
647	    const int nsamp = nrows / mb::kSeq;
648	
649	    // ── CE bwd + scalar head + final-norm bwd, per sample. dh (last-layer output
650	    //    adjoint) → sc.work_d (zero non-last rows). ──
651	    for (int idx = threadIdx.x; idx < nrows * mb::kD; idx += blockDim.x) sc.work_d[idx] = 0.0f;
652	    __syncthreads();
653	    for (int si = 0; si < nsamp; ++si) {
654	        const int rlast = si * mb::kSeq + (mb::kSeq - 1);
655	        const int gs = g0 / mb::kSeq + si;
656	        float* lg = sc.logits + (int64_t)si * mb::kPHead;
657	        int tgt = tgt_ids[gs];
658	        float lmax = -CUDART_INF_F;
659	        for (int o = threadIdx.x; o < mb::kPHead; o += blockDim.x) lmax = fmaxf(lmax, lg[o]);
660	        lmax = mb_block_max(lmax, red);
661	        float es = 0.0f;
662	        for (int o = threadIdx.x; o < mb::kPHead; o += blockDim.x) es += __expf(lg[o] - lmax);
663	        es = mb_block_sum(es, red);
664	        float inv_es = 1.0f / es;
665	        // dlogits → overwrite lg (scalar head, fp32; NO bf16 — head is not a projection).
666	        for (int o = threadIdx.x; o < mb::kPHead; o += blockDim.x) {
667	            float smo = __expf(lg[o] - lmax) * inv_es;
668	            lg[o] = (smo - ((o == tgt) ? 1.0f : 0.0f)) / (float)B;
669	        }
670	        __syncthreads();
671	        // head: out_b += dl ; out_w[o] += dl * hn  (hn = fn_xhat*norm_w + norm_b).
672	        const float* xh = sc.fn_xhat + (int64_t)rlast * mb::kD;
673	        for (int o = threadIdx.x; o < mb::kPHead; o += blockDim.x) {
674	            float dl = lg[o];
675	            part.out_b[o] += dl;
676	            float* gwrow = part.out_w + (int64_t)o * mb::kD;
677	            #pragma unroll 4
678	            for (int j = 0; j < mb::kD; ++j) gwrow[j] += dl * (xh[j] * w.norm_w[j] + w.norm_b[j]);
679	        }
680	        __syncthreads();
681	        // dhn[j] = Σ_o dl[o]*out_w[o,j] → sc.work_di row 0 (transient; d-wide).
682	        for (int j = threadIdx.x; j < mb::kD; j += blockDim.x) {
683	            float acc = 0.0f;
684	            for (int o = 0; o < mb::kPHead; ++o) acc += lg[o] * w.out_w[(int64_t)o * mb::kD + j];
685	            sc.work_di[j] = acc;   // dhn (reuse work_di[0..d) as transient)
686	        }
687	        __syncthreads();
688	        // final-norm bwd (single row last): norm γ/β → partial; dh[rlast] = LN-dx.
689	        for (int j = threadIdx.x; j < mb::kD; j += blockDim.x) {
690	            float d = sc.work_di[j];
691	            part.norm_b[j] += d; part.norm_w[j] += d * xh[j];
692	        }
693	        __syncthreads();
694	        {
695	            float sda = 0.0f, sdax = 0.0f;
696	            for (int j = threadIdx.x; j < mb::kD; j += blockDim.x) {
697	                float dxhat = sc.work_di[j] * w.norm_w[j]; sda += dxhat; sdax += dxhat * xh[j];
698	            }
699	            sda = mb_block_sum(sda, red); sdax = mb_block_sum(sdax, red);
700	            float iv = sc.fn_inv[rlast];
701	            for (int j = threadIdx.x; j < mb::kD; j += blockDim.x) {
702	                float dxhat = sc.work_di[j] * w.norm_w[j];
703	                sc.work_d[(int64_t)rlast * mb::kD + j] = iv * (dxhat - (sda + xh[j] * sdax) / (float)mb::kD);
704	            }
705	            __syncthreads();
706	        }
707	    }
708	    // sc.work_d now = dh (grad wrt last-layer output [nrows,d], only last pos nonzero).
709	
710	    for (int li = mb::kLayers - 1; li >= 0; --li) {
711	        const MambaWeights::Layer& L = w.layer[li];
712	        // (the residual operand layer_in is read by P2's in_proj dW from acts.X_in[li];
713	        //  the residual ADJOINT path here is the saved dr in sc.work_d.)
714	        // (1) LN bwd (per-sample): dh → dr (sc.work_di2 reused as dr, d-wide);
715	        //     accumulate per-layer norm γ/β into partial.
716	        for (int si = 0; si < nsamp; ++si) {
717	            MambaSampleSmem::LayerAct* a = &sc.act[li][si];
718	            const int r0 = si * mb::kSeq;
719	            mb_layernorm_bwd(sc.work_d + (int64_t)r0 * mb::kD, &a->ln_xhat[0][0], &a->ln_inv[0],
720	                             L.n_w, sc.work_di2 + (int64_t)r0 * mb::kD, part.n_w[li], part.n_b[li], red);
721	        }
722	        // dr lives in sc.work_di2[:, :d]. (2) r = y_out + residual:
723	        //   dy_out = dr ; dx_residual = dr (SAVE dx_residual into sc.work_d — dh free now).

425	    c["grad_checkpoint"] = False

429	    # ZERO FLOPs. With use_fused=True on the L3 cells (decoder/vit/mamba × adamw

439	    with profile(activities=[ProfilerActivity.CUDA, ProfilerActivity.CPU],

528	def _build_tc_module(model, verbose=False):
529	    """JIT-build the model's TC TU (mirrors the test _build_tc_module: 9.0a,
530	    -O3 -std=c++17 --expt-relaxed-constexpr, sm_90a gencode). Cached per model.
531	    Raises on build failure (the caller skips TC rows per the owner's "skip if
532	    JIT-path still blocked")."""
533	    import os
534	    if model in _TC_MOD_CACHE:
535	        return _TC_MOD_CACHE[model]
536	    os.environ["TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST"] = "9.0a"
537	    from torch.utils.cpp_extension import load
538	    tu = str(ROOT / _TC_TU_REL[model])
539	    mod = load(
540	        name=f"mega_{model}_real_adamw_tc",
541	        sources=[tu], extra_include_paths=[str(ROOT)],
542	        extra_cuda_cflags=[
543	            "-O3", "-std=c++17", "--expt-relaxed-constexpr",
544	            "-gencode=arch=compute_90a,code=sm_90a",
545	            "-gencode=arch=compute_90a,code=compute_90a", "-lineinfo"],
546	        extra_cflags=["-O3", "-std=c++17"], verbose=verbose)
547	    _TC_MOD_CACHE[model] = mod
548	    return mod

551	def _tc_inputs(model, B, dev):
552	    """Per-model (params, input, targets) for one TC/scalar step at batch B. The
553	    flat params are random of the TC TU's TOTAL size — step TIME is independent of
554	    param VALUES (correctness is already validated by the cells' gates: decoder
555	    13/13+5, vit 21/21, mamba 5/5), so we don't need the exact named layout here.
556	    decoder/mamba take int32 tokens [B,seq]; vit takes float32 patches [B,16,49]."""
557	    import torch
558	    mod = _build_tc_module(model)
559	    total = int(mod.TOTAL)
560	    gpar = torch.Generator(device=dev).manual_seed(42)
561	    params = (torch.randn(total, generator=gpar, device=dev) * 0.02).contiguous()
562	    gin = torch.Generator(device=dev).manual_seed(7)
563	    if model == "vit":
564	        from tests.hw.vit_oracle import NUM_PATCHES, PATCH_DIM, VOCAB
565	        inp = torch.randn(B, NUM_PATCHES, PATCH_DIM, generator=gin, device=dev).to(torch.float32)
566	        tgt = torch.randint(0, VOCAB, (B,), generator=gin, device=dev).to(torch.int32)
567	    elif model == "mamba":
568	        from tests.hw.mamba_oracle import VOCAB, P_HEAD, SEQ
569	        inp = torch.randint(0, VOCAB, (B, SEQ), generator=gin, device=dev).to(torch.int32)
570	        tgt = torch.randint(0, P_HEAD, (B,), generator=gin, device=dev).to(torch.int32)
571	    else:  # decoder
572	        from tests.hw.decoder_oracle import VOCAB, SEQ
573	        inp = torch.randint(0, VOCAB, (B, SEQ), generator=gin, device=dev).to(torch.int32)
574	        tgt = torch.randint(0, VOCAB, (B,), generator=gin, device=dev).to(torch.int32)
575	    return mod, params, inp, tgt, total

578	def _time_tc_kernel(call, warmup=8, iters=40):
579	    import torch
580	    for _ in range(warmup):
581	        call()
582	    torch.cuda.synchronize()
583	    t0 = time.perf_counter()
584	    for _ in range(iters):
585	        call()
586	    torch.cuda.synchronize()
587	    return (time.perf_counter() - t0) / iters

590	def measure_tc_cell(model, eager_flops_full, eager_B_full, n_params,
591	                    seq, dim, layers):
592	    """Measure the directly-loaded TC TU for `model` (Task 2) AND its scalar
593	    sibling (Task 3) at the same B%16 full batch, ncta_cap=0 (full saturation).
594	
595	    eager_flops_full / eager_B_full: FLOPs/step and batch from the eager adamw
596	    profile (pass 3 of measure_pipeline, use_fused=False — the path-independent
597	    GEMM count). FLOPs scale linearly in B, so flops_at(B) = eager_flops_full ·
598	    B / eager_B_full. Returns a list of two rows (tc, scalar) or [] if the JIT
599	    build is blocked.
600	    """
601	    import torch
602	    dev = torch.device("cuda")
603	    B = eager_B_full - (eager_B_full % 16)          # decoder TC requires B%16==0
604	    try:
605	        mod, params, inp, tgt, total = _tc_inputs(model, B, dev)
606	    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 — JIT blocked → owner says skip TC rows
607	        print(f"  TC[{model}] BUILD/SETUP FAILED (skipping TC rows): {e}", flush=True)
608	        return []
609	    torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 = False
610	    torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32 = False
611	    flops_per_step = eager_flops_full * (B / float(eager_B_full))
612	    beta1, beta2 = 0.9, 0.98
613	    bc1, bc2 = 1.0 - beta1, 1.0 - beta2
614	    lr, eps, wd = 1e-3, 1e-8, 0.0
615	    state = torch.zeros(3 * total, dtype=torch.float32, device=dev)
616	
617	    def _tc_call():
618	        return mod.tc_train_step(params.clone(), inp, tgt, state, lr, beta1, beta2,
619	                                 eps, wd, bc1, bc2, 1, 0)
620	    def _sc_call():
621	        return mod.scalar_train_step(params.clone(), inp, tgt, state, lr, beta1,
622	                                     beta2, eps, wd, bc1, bc2, 1)
623	
624	    rows = []
625	    for label, family, prec, call, has in (
626	        ("tc_train_step",     "tc",     "bf16-TC", _tc_call, True),
627	        ("scalar_train_step", "scalar-mega", "fp32", _sc_call,
628	         hasattr(mod, "scalar_train_step")),
629	    ):
630	        if not has:
631	            continue
632	        try:
633	            wall = _time_tc_kernel(call)
634	        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
635	            print(f"  TC[{model}] {label} FAILED: {e}", flush=True)
636	            continue
637	        # Bytes/AI: keep the SAME analytical traffic model as the scalar rows for
638	        # cross-row comparability (adamw S=2), BUT the TC kernel stores activations
639	        # in bf16 (2B not 4B). The activation term dominates at these B, so an
640	        # all-fp32 byte model understates TC AI ~2×. We report BOTH: the fp32-model
641	        # AI (comparable to every other row) and a TC-faithful AI (activations 2B).
642	        # CAVEAT (load-bearing): the TC point lands MEMORY-bound in this analytical
643	        # model (AI·BW < bf16 peak), so the ceiling — and thus the fraction —
644	        # depends on this byte assumption. The achieved TF/s (the honest axis) does
645	        # NOT. The writeup leads with achieved TF/s and reports BOTH AIs for TC.
646	        bps_fp32 = bytes_per_step("adamw", model, n_params, B, seq, dim, layers)
647	        # TC-faithful: halve the activation byte term (acts stored bf16).
648	        acts = B * seq * dim * layers * (10 if model == "mamba" else 14)
649	        bps_tc = bps_fp32 - 2 * 4.0 * acts + 2 * 2.0 * acts  # acts 4B→2B
650	        bps = bps_tc if family == "tc" else bps_fp32
651	        achieved = flops_per_step / wall
652	        ai = flops_per_step / bps
653	        ai_fp32model = flops_per_step / bps_fp32
654	        peak_c = PEAKS["bf16_tc"] if family == "tc" else PEAKS["fp32_cuda"]
655	        ceiling = min(peak_c, ai * PEAKS["hbm_bw"])
656	        bound = "compute" if peak_c < ai * PEAKS["hbm_bw"] else "memory"
657	        rows.append({
658	            "optimizer": "adamw", "model": model,
659	            "precision": prec, "use_amp": False,
660	            "path": f"L3-real-megakernel({label})", "path_family": family,
661	            "tc_batch": B, "ncta_cap": 0,
662	            "steps_per_s": 1.0 / wall, "wall_per_step_ms": wall * 1e3,
663	            "flops_per_step": flops_per_step,
664	            "flops_basis": "eager-profiled (use_fused=False) scaled by B/B_full",
665	            "bytes_per_step_analytical": bps,
666	            "bytes_model": ("tc-faithful (acts bf16 2B)" if family == "tc"
667	                            else "fp32 (all 4B)"),
668	            "achieved_flops_per_s": achieved,
669	            "arithmetic_intensity": ai,
670	            "arithmetic_intensity_fp32model": ai_fp32model,
671	            "matmul_peak_used": peak_c,
672	            "roofline_ceiling_flops_per_s": ceiling,
673	            "fraction_of_roofline": achieved / ceiling,
674	            "bound_regime_at_AI": bound,
675	            "achieved_bytes_per_s_analytical": bps / wall,
676	            "fraction_of_hbm_bw": (bps / wall) / PEAKS["hbm_bw"],

781	def _delta_vs_baseline(rows, baseline_path):
782	    """[ROOFLINE-DELTA] Diff the new scalar rows against the archived eager
783	    baseline (same (optimizer, model) key, path_family scalar). Reports the change
784	    in roofline-fraction / achieved-TF/s / precision/path so the owner can see what
785	    moved when the L3 megakernel actually fired."""
786	    try:
787	        base = json.loads(Path(baseline_path).read_text())
788	    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
789	        return []
790	    bmap = {(r["optimizer"], r["model"]): r
791	            for r in base.get("rows", []) if r.get("path_family", "scalar") == "scalar"}
792	    out = []
793	    for r in rows:
794	        if r.get("path_family", "scalar") != "scalar":
795	            continue                       # deltas only defined for the scalar race rows
796	        b = bmap.get((r["optimizer"], r["model"]))
797	        if not b:
798	            continue
799	        # [ROOFLINE-DELTA] Decompose WHY the fraction moved (advisor): a fraction
800	        # jump can come from (a) a real PATH change (adamw: eager+L1 → L3 real
801	        # megakernel) or (b) a pure CEILING relabel (the other opts only changed
802	        # precision bf16→fp32, dropping the ceiling 285→66.9 TF, so the same
803	        # achieved TF/s reads as a higher fraction — NOT more efficient). We record
804	        # the OLD path + a path_changed flag + the ceiling ratio so the writeup
805	        # never implies fp32 made 10 optimizers faster (it did not).
806	        # The eager baseline predates path labelling AND the extension build fix
807	        # (per the commit timeline the fused path was broken then → every baseline
808	        # row ran eager / eager+L1). So "did the PATH genuinely change" = did the
809	        # NEW row fire the L3-real megakernel (the only path this fp32-force newly
810	        # enables). The non-adamw rows ran eager+L1 in BOTH (ceiling-relabel only).
811	        path_old = b.get("path") or "eager (unlabelled pre-fix)"
812	        # A real L3 megakernel fired iff the path starts "L3-" (now "L3-TC-..."/
813	        # "L3-scalar-..." after the bf16/wgmma wiring; was "L3-real-..." pre-wiring).
814	        path_changed = str(r.get("path", "")).startswith("L3-")
815	        ceil_old = b.get("roofline_ceiling_flops_per_s", 0.0) or 0.0
816	        ceil_new = r.get("roofline_ceiling_flops_per_s", 0.0) or 0.0
817	        tf_old = b.get("achieved_flops_per_s", 0) / 1e12
818	        tf_new = r.get("achieved_flops_per_s", 0) / 1e12
819	        out.append({
820	            "optimizer": r["optimizer"], "model": r["model"],
821	            "precision_old": b.get("precision"), "precision_new": r.get("precision"),
822	            "path_old": path_old, "path_new": r.get("path"),
823	            "path_changed": path_changed,
824	            "roof_frac_old": b.get("fraction_of_roofline"),
825	            "roof_frac_new": r.get("fraction_of_roofline"),
826	            "roof_frac_delta": (r.get("fraction_of_roofline", 0)
827	                                - b.get("fraction_of_roofline", 0)),
828	            "achieved_tf_old": tf_old, "achieved_tf_new": tf_new,
829	            "achieved_tf_ratio_new_over_old": (tf_new / tf_old) if tf_old else None,
830	            "ceiling_tf_old": ceil_old / 1e12, "ceiling_tf_new": ceil_new / 1e12,
831	            "ceiling_ratio_old_over_new": (ceil_old / ceil_new) if ceil_new else None,
832	            "steps_per_s_old": b.get("steps_per_s"),
833	            "steps_per_s_new": r.get("steps_per_s"),
834	            # the honest tag: did the underlying WORK change, or just the ceiling label?
835	            "interpretation": ("PATH CHANGED (real megakernel now measured)"
836	                               if path_changed else
837	                               "ceiling-relabel only (precision changed, work same)"),
838	        })
839	    return out

input.content:
"""Differential-bypass profiler for the Mamba TC megakernel (mamba-lane bottleneck).

ncu SpeedOfLight is blocked in this container (ERR_NVGPUCTRPERM), so we attribute
wall to phases by NULLING OUT one phase at a time (compile-time -D flags, default-0
so the shipped kernel is unchanged) and timing the delta. Quiet GPU
(CUDA_MPS_PIPE_DIRECTORY=/nonexistent), B=16384, ncta_cap=0 (one CTA/SM = shipped).

Run: CUDA_MPS_PIPE_DIRECTORY=/nonexistent PYTHONPATH=. python tuning/_mbtc_bypass_profile.py
"""
import os, sys, time, json
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
import torch
os.environ["TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST"] = "9.0a"
from torch.utils.cpp_extension import load
from tests.hw.mamba_oracle import VOCAB, P_HEAD, SEQ

B = int(os.environ.get("MBTC_B", "16384"))
B -= B % 16
TU = os.path.join(ROOT, "csrc/fused/sm_90/mega_mamba_real_adamw_tc.cu")


def build(name, extra_defs):
    flags = ["-O3", "-std=c++17", "--expt-relaxed-constexpr",
             "-gencode=arch=compute_90a,code=sm_90a",
             "-gencode=arch=compute_90a,code=compute_90a", "-lineinfo"]
    flags += [f"-D{d}" for d in extra_defs]
    return load(name=name, sources=[TU], extra_include_paths=[ROOT],
                extra_cuda_cflags=flags, extra_cflags=["-O3", "-std=c++17"],
                verbose=False)


def time_call(call, warmup=8, iters=40):
    for _ in range(warmup):
        call()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    for _ in range(iters):
        call()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    return (time.perf_counter() - t0) / iters * 1e3   # ms


def main():
    dev = torch.device("cuda")
    torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 = False
    # Variants: name -> list of -D defines. mod_<name> is a distinct JIT module.
    variants = {
        "baseline":     [],
        "no_dw_gemm":   ["SG_MBTC_BYPASS_DW_GEMM=1"],
        "no_scan":      ["SG_MBTC_BYPASS_SCAN=1"],
        "no_embedscan": ["SG_MBTC_BYPASS_EMBED_SCAN=1"],
        "no_proj_fwd":  ["SG_MBTC_BYPASS_PROJ_FWD=1"],
    }
    print(f"[mbtc-bypass] B={B}  T={B*SEQ}  quiet={os.environ.get('CUDA_MPS_PIPE_DIRECTORY')}")
    results = {}
    base_ms = None
    base_sc_ms = None
    for name, defs in variants.items():
        try:
            mod = build(f"mbtc_bp_{name}", defs)
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"  {name:14s} BUILD FAILED: {str(e)[:200]}")
            continue
        total = int(mod.TOTAL)
        gpar = torch.Generator(device=dev).manual_seed(42)
        params = (torch.randn(total, generator=gpar, device=dev) * 0.02).contiguous()
        gin = torch.Generator(device=dev).manual_seed(7)
        inp = torch.randint(0, VOCAB, (B, SEQ), generator=gin, device=dev).to(torch.int32)
        tgt = torch.randint(0, P_HEAD, (B,), generator=gin, device=dev).to(torch.int32)
        state = torch.zeros(3 * total, dtype=torch.float32, device=dev)
        beta1, beta2 = 0.9, 0.98
        bc1, bc2 = 1.0 - beta1, 1.0 - beta2

        def tc_call():
            return mod.tc_train_step(params.clone(), inp, tgt, state, 1e-3, beta1, beta2,
                                     1e-8, 0.0, bc1, bc2, 1, 0)
        ms = time_call(tc_call)
        results[name] = {"tc_ms": ms}
        if name == "baseline":
            base_ms = ms
            # scalar baseline from the SAME module (back-to-back, same contention)
            def sc_call():
                return mod.scalar_train_step(params.clone(), inp, tgt, state, 1e-3, beta1,
                                             beta2, 1e-8, 0.0, bc1, bc2, 1)
            base_sc_ms = time_call(sc_call)
            results["scalar_baseline"] = {"tc_ms": base_sc_ms}
            print(f"  {'baseline (TC)':18s} {ms:8.3f} ms")
            print(f"  {'baseline (scalar)':18s} {base_sc_ms:8.3f} ms   "
                  f"(scalar/TC = {base_sc_ms/ms:.3f}x; TC must beat 1.0 to win)")
        else:
            delta = base_ms - ms
            pct = 100.0 * delta / base_ms
            print(f"  {name:18s} {ms:8.3f} ms   phase≈{delta:7.3f} ms ({pct:5.1f}% of TC wall)")
    out = os.path.join(ROOT, "results/h100_grokking_race/mbtc_bypass_profile.json")
    json.dump({"B": B, "T": B*SEQ, "baseline_tc_ms": base_ms,
               "baseline_scalar_ms": base_sc_ms, "variants": results}, open(out, "w"), indent=2)
    print(f"[mbtc-bypass] wrote {out}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

**Split-K dW design (the named "multi-CTA tiling"):**
Currently each dW output tile (gt) is owned by one CTA which contracts the full K=T. With ~36 tiles over 132 SMs, ~96 idle.

Split-K: partition K=T into `G` chunks. Make each work item a `(output-tile, k-chunk)` pair → `n_dw * G` work items, distributed `% nCTA`. Each CTA computes a PARTIAL dW over its k-chunk, accumulates into a per-(tile, chunk) scratch slot. Then a grid barrier, then a deterministic reduction summing the G partials per output tile in ascending chunk order into `grad`.

Choosing G: to fill 132 SMs with 36 tiles, G≈4 gives 144 work items ≈ full occupancy. The k-chunk size = T/G = 131072/4 = 32768 = 2048 k-steps each. The reduction adds a small cost (G floats per output element).

Determinism: the partial accumulation within a chunk is ascending-k (unchanged); the cross-chunk reduction sums chunk 0,1,...,G-1 in fixed ascending order → deterministic, no float atomics.

The most likely bug: **the split-K reduce writes to grad, but the grad was NOT zeroed, and the single-CTA path also... no.** Actually — the ISO test calls `tc_dump_outproj_operands` which reads the kernel's stored bf16 acts and recomputes the dW in fp32, comparing to the kernel's grad. If the kernel's grad is ~2× the correct, rel≈1.0.

**~2× suggests double-counting.** Where? In the partial pass, each (gt, kc) is computed by `item = cta; item < n_dw*kDwG; item += nCTA`. With ncta_cap=8 and n_dw*G=144 items, each item computed once. The reduce sums G=4 chunks. If the chunks OVERLAP in their k-ranges (each covering more than T/G), I'd double-count. `kc_steps = k_steps_total/G`, `k0 = kc*kc_steps`, chunk covers [k0, k0+kc_steps). For G=4, kc=0..3, chunks [0,kc_steps),[kc_steps,2kc_steps),... — NON-overlapping, covering [0, 4*kc_steps) = [0, k_steps_total). ✓ No overlap.

Hmm. Let me think about the **out accessor in the partial**: `slot[m*N + n]`. N is the template param SG_TUNED_TILE_N=128. The slot stride is `kMbDwTileFloats = 64*kMbMaxTileN = 64*128`. Let me look more carefully — maybe the bug is that `mbtc_dw_run_tile_splitk`'s `out` writes `slot[m*N+n]` but the slot pointer `dw_part + ((gt*G+kc)*kMbDwTileFloats)` — and `kMbDwTileFloats = 64*kMbMaxTileN`. I'm not spotting it by inspection. Let me consult the advisor with the specific failure signature (deterministic, rel~1.0 ≈ 2× double-count, ISO-isolated to the dW GEMM, trajectory still descends). The advisor saw my split-K code. Let me get their read on the bug.

Found it. It's a one-line indexing bug in the split-K partial write — not double-counting. Verify this before anything else:

**`mbtc_dw_run_tile_splitk`'s `out` accessor indexes the slot by the GLOBAL row, but the slot holds only 64 LOCAL rows.**

```cpp
const int mbase = m_atom * 64;     // 0, 64, 128, ...
...
auto out = [&](int m, int n, float v) {
    if (m < 64 && n < N) slot[(int64_t)m * N + n] = v; };
```

`tc_gemm_block_unpipelined` calls `out(mbase + row, col, ...)`. So `m = mbase + row`. For any tile with `m_atom >= 1` (mbase ≥ 64), the guard `m < 64` is **false for every row → the entire slot is never written.** The reduce then reads stale/zero memory for those tiles.

**This matches every symptom exactly:**
- `in_proj` (Nout=512 → 8 m-atoms): only m_atom 0 written, 7/8 garbage → worst tensor, rel 1.0. ✓
- `out_proj` (Nout=128 → 2 m-atoms): upper half zero. ISO `max|err|=3.7e-4` *equals the reference magnitude* → kernel≈0 on those rows, not 2×. ✓ (Your "~2× double-count" read is wrong — it's **missing writes**, kernel→0 on upper atoms.)
- Determinism passes: suppressed writes are deterministic. ✓ (Exactly the trap — gate 3 can't see it; gates 1+2 caught it, as intended.)
- Trajectory still descends: the m_atom=0 half of every weight gets correct grads. ✓
- layer0 ≈ layer1 rel (~0.7 each): systematic across all multi-atom proj weights, not a layer-specific issue. ✓

**The fix — index by local row (`m - mbase`):**
```cpp
auto out = [&](int m, int n, float v) {
    const int lr = m - mbase;                       // local row in this atom's 64-row slot
    if (lr >= 0 && lr < 64 && n < N) slot[(int64_t)lr * N + n] = v; };
```
`srcA` must keep using global `m` (it reads `dY[... * Nout + m]` — the correct dY row), so you can't pass `mbase0=0`. Only the slot write is local. The **reduce is already correct** (it writes `grad[(mbase+row)*Kin...]` global, reads `slot[row*N+col]` local) — single-site fix.

**This does not invalidate split-K.** The design is right; this is a transcription error, not a structural problem. After the fix, every read slot region is fully written, so you still don't need to zero `dw_part`.

Critical: the production wgmma path truncates B to the **largest multiple of 16** (`B_tc = B - (B % 16)`), NOT 64. So for the race (decoder ~4191 train pairs), B_tc = 4191 - (4191%16) = 4191 - 15 = 4176. Is 4176 % 64 == 0? 4176/64 = 65.25 → NO. So with G=4 requiring B%64==0, the production decoder cells would get `cudaErrorInvalidValue` → dispatch throws → **the production lion/adamw/grokfast decoder cells BREAK.**

This is a regression I must prevent. The fix: relax the split-K to handle B%16 (not B%64). The constraint is G | (B/16) for the head (K=B). With B%16==0, B/16 is an integer, but may not be divisible by G=4 (e.g., B/16=261 for B=4176, 261%4=1). 

Options:
1. **Make G adaptive**: use the largest G ∈ {1,2,4} that divides B/16 (and T/16). At runtime, pick G = gcd-compatible. But G is compile-time (template/macro).
2. **Make the split-K handle unequal/remainder chunks**: instead of requiring G | (K/16), let the last chunk absorb the remainder. This is more robust.
3. **Fall back to G=1 (single-CTA) when B/16 not divisible by G** — but then the production cells get no speedup (just correctness).

Option 2 (remainder-handling chunks) is the most robust and keeps the speedup for all B. Let me redesign the chunk split to handle remainders: `kc_steps = ceil((K/16)/G)`, and the last chunks may have fewer steps (or zero). Each chunk covers `[kc*kc_steps, min((kc+1)*kc_steps, K/16))`. Chunks beyond the range do nothing.

Floor-balanced has no empty chunks down to KS≥G:

const int k1 = (int)(((int64_t)(kc + 1) * KS) / G);
const int kc_steps = k1 - k0;               // near-equal, sums to KS exactly
// token offset into dY/X is k0 * 16  (replaces kc*kc_steps*16)

"""
import os, sys
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))


def main():
    print("=" * 70, flush=True)
    print("[decoder-validate] (1) wiring_check --models decoder", flush=True)
    print("=" * 70, flush=True)
    import wiring_check as wc
    rows = []
    for opt in wc.OPTS:
        r = wc.check_cell(opt, "decoder", steps=4)
        rows.append(r)
        mark = "PASS L3-TC" if r["is_l3_tc"] else "BLOCKED   "
        print(f"  [{mark}] {opt:11s}/decoder  path={r['executed_path']:26s}", flush=True)
    conv = [r for r in rows if r["is_l3_tc"]]
    print(f"  => decoder L3-TC: {len(conv)}/{len(rows)} "
          f"(converted: {[r['optimizer'] for r in conv]})", flush=True)

    print("\n" + "=" * 70, flush=True)
    print("[decoder-validate] (2) tail_gate adamw/lion/grokfast/decoder", flush=True)
    print("=" * 70, flush=True)
    from tests.hw.test_l3tc_tail_gate import run_cell_gate
    tg = {}
    for cell in ("adamw/decoder", "lion/decoder", "grokfast/decoder"):
        try:
            ok, detail = run_cell_gate(cell, verbose=True)
            tg[cell] = ok
            print(f"  => {cell}: {'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}\n", flush=True)
        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
            tg[cell] = False
            import traceback; traceback.print_exc()
            print(f"  => {cell}: ERROR {e}\n", flush=True)

    print("\n" + "=" * 70, flush=True)
    print("[decoder-validate] (3) decoder TC TF/s re-measure (B=16384, ncta=0)", flush=True)
    print("=" * 70, flush=True)
    from tuning.roofline import measure_tc_cell, _data_init
    import json
    ef, eb = 4.23e10, 16384   # fallback FLOP basis (same as baseline for relative cmp)
    try:
        d = json.load(open("results/h100_grokking_race/roofline.json"))
        row = next((r for r in d["rows"] if r["optimizer"] == "adamw"
                    and r["model"] == "decoder" and r.get("path_family") == "scalar"), None)
        if row and row.get("flops_per_step"):
            ef, eb = row["flops_per_step"], row["batch"]
    except Exception:
        pass
    npar = _data_init("decoder")[2]
    trows = measure_tc_cell("decoder", ef, eb, npar, 4, 128, 2)
    for r in trows:
        print(f"  DECODER {r['path_family']:11s}: {r['wall_per_step_ms']:.3f} ms  "
              f"{r['achieved_flops_per_s']/1e12:.3f} TF/s  roof%={100*r['fraction_of_roofline']:.2f}",
              flush=True)

    print("\n[decoder-validate] SUMMARY:", flush=True)
    print(f"  wiring_check L3-TC: {len(conv)}/{len(rows)}", flush=True)
    print(f"  tail_gate: {tg}", flush=True)
    allok = len(conv) >= 3 and all(tg.values())
    print(f"  => {'ALL GREEN' if allok else 'NEEDS ATTENTION'}", flush=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

1	#pragma once
2	// GrokAdamW — vendor-neutral algorithm header.
3	//
4	// Reference: Lee et al. 2024, "GrokAdamW: A Faster Optimizer for Late
5	// Generalization" — AdamW with an EMA gradient filter that amplifies
6	// persistent directions (the slow-changing components of the gradient
7	// signal).
8	//
9	// Math (decoupled weight decay variant; bias correction via division):
10	//   ema_t = alpha * ema_{t-1} + (1 - alpha) * g
11	//   g_amp = g + lamb * ema_t
12	//   m_t   = beta1 * m_{t-1} + (1 - beta1) * g_amp
13	//   v_t   = beta2 * v_{t-1} + (1 - beta2) * g_amp^2
14	//   m_hat = m_t / (1 - beta1^t)
15	//   v_hat = v_t / (1 - beta2^t)
16	//   p    -= lr * (m_hat / (sqrt(v_hat) + eps) + wd * p)
17	//
18	// Calling convention: bc1, bc2 are passed un-inverted —
19	//   bc1 = 1 - beta1^t,  bc2 = 1 - beta2^t.
20	
21	#include "csrc/common/types.h"
22	#include "csrc/common/utils.cuh"
23	
24	namespace sg { namespace algorithms {
25	
26	template <typename ParamT, typename GradT>
27	__device__ __forceinline__ void grokadamw_step(
28	    ParamT* __restrict__ param,
29	    float* __restrict__ exp_avg,
30	    float* __restrict__ exp_avg_sq,
31	    float* __restrict__ ema,
32	    const GradT* __restrict__ grad,
33	    const float alpha,    // EMA decay (e.g. 0.98)
34	    const float lamb,     // amplification factor (e.g. 5.0)
35	    const float lr,
36	    const float beta1,
37	    const float beta2,
38	    const float eps,
39	    const float wd,
40	    const float bc1,
41	    const float bc2,
42	    const int64_t idx
43	) {
44	    const float g = static_cast<float>(grad[idx]);
45	    const float p = static_cast<float>(param[idx]);
46	
47	    // EMA filter
48	    const float ema_new = alpha * ema[idx] + (1.0f - alpha) * g;
49	    ema[idx] = ema_new;
50	
51	    // Amplified gradient
52	    const float g_amp = g + lamb * ema_new;
53	
54	    // Adam moments
55	    const float m = beta1 * exp_avg[idx]    + (1.0f - beta1) * g_amp;
56	    const float v = beta2 * exp_avg_sq[idx] + (1.0f - beta2) * g_amp * g_amp;
57	    exp_avg[idx]    = m;
58	    exp_avg_sq[idx] = v;
59	
60	    // Bias-corrected update with decoupled weight decay.
61	    // bc1, bc2 are passed un-inverted (= 1 - beta^t), so divide.
62	    const float update = (m / sg_safe_bc(bc1)) / (sqrtf(v / sg_safe_bc(bc2)) + eps);
63	    param[idx] = static_cast<ParamT>(p - lr * (update + wd * p));
64	}
65	
66	// Canonical bias-corrected Adam tail on a caller-supplied effective gradient
67	// g_eff. This is the SINGLE source of the moment-update + decoupled-WD apply
68	// math, factored out of grokadamw_step so storage-variant kernels (e.g. the
69	// quantized Config-3 path, which dequantizes/requantizes the state) can reuse
70	// the exact same float ops without re-inlining them. Produces m_out, v_out
71	// (the new moments) and p_out (the new parameter value) by reference; the
72	// caller is responsible for writing them back (FP32 or quantized).
73	//
74	// Bit-identical to the tail of grokadamw_step:
75	//   m = beta1 * m_prev + (1 - beta1) * g_eff;
76	//   v = beta2 * v_prev + (1 - beta2) * g_eff * g_eff;
77	//   update = (m / bc1) / (sqrtf(v / bc2) + eps);
78	//   p_out  = p - lr * (update + wd * p);
79	__device__ __forceinline__ void grokadamw_adam_tail(
80	    const float g_eff,
81	    const float p,
82	    const float m_prev,
83	    const float v_prev,
84	    const float lr,
85	    const float beta1,
86	    const float beta2,
87	    const float eps,
88	    const float wd,
89	    const float bc1,
90	    const float bc2,
91	    float& m_out,
92	    float& v_out,
93	    float& p_out
94	) {
95	    const float m = beta1 * m_prev + (1.0f - beta1) * g_eff;
96	    const float v = beta2 * v_prev + (1.0f - beta2) * g_eff * g_eff;
97	    const float update = (m / sg_safe_bc(bc1)) / (sqrtf(v / sg_safe_bc(bc2)) + eps);
98	    m_out = m;
99	    v_out = v;
100	    p_out = p - lr * (update + wd * p);
101	}
102	
103	}} // namespace sg::algorithms

1	"""
2	GrokAdamW — Adam with grokking-aware EMA gradient filtering and amplification.
3	
4	Combines AdamW with an exponential moving average (EMA) gradient filter that
5	detects and amplifies slow-learning gradient signals, accelerating the
6	transition from memorisation to generalisation (grokking).
7	
8	This is the PUBLISHED GrokAdamW algorithm (QuixiAI/grokadamw aka
9	cognitivecomputations/grokadamw; also HF transformers PR #32521). Two
10	mechanisms beyond plain EMA-filtered AdamW make it "grokking-aware", BOTH wired
11	here (they were previously dead constructor args):
12	
13	  (1) LAYER-WISE β1 MOMENTUM DECAY.  Per the reference (grokadamw.py):
14	          layer_beta1 = beta1 * (1 - gamma) ** i
15	      where ``i`` is the enumeration index of the parameter tensor. Earlier
16	      layers keep the full β1; later layers get a progressively smaller β1
17	      (less momentum), which the paper motivates as promoting early-layer
18	      generalisation. gamma default 0.1. Implemented with the SAME flat-index
19	      pattern as supergrok11.py's ``_flat_layer_beta1s``.
20	
21	  (2) GROKKING-SIGNAL-DRIVEN ADAPTIVE α.  α is the EMA decay of the slow-grad
22	      filter; the reference modulates it from a grokking signal. VERBATIM from
23	      the reference (grokadamw.py):
24	          # _default_grokking_signal(train_loss, eval_loss):
25	          diff      = max(0, eval_loss - train_loss)
26	          max_loss  = max(eval_loss, train_loss)
27	          signal    = diff / max_loss if max_loss > 0 else 0.0
28	          # then, per param-group:
29	          alpha = alpha_init * math.exp(-grokking_signal_decay_rate * signal)
30	      i.e. ALPHA SCHEDULE  α_t = alpha_init · exp(−κ · signal),  with the
31	      signal the *max-normalised* (NOT train-normalised) clipped val−train gap
32	      and κ == ``grokking_signal_decay_rate`` (default 0.1). The slow-grad
33	      filter + amplification it feeds is unchanged and identical to the kernel
34	      math (csrc/algorithms/grokadamw.h):
35	          grok_ema  = α·grok_ema + (1−α)·grad
36	          grok_grad = grad + lamb·grok_ema
37	      lamb default 2.0 in the reference. (Our historical default was 5.0; we
38	      keep the constructor default at the reference value 2.0 — see __init__.)
39	
40	INTERPRETATION / SOURCE NOTES (read LOUDLY):
41	  * The reference α update lives in ``_default_grokking_signal`` +
42	    the per-group ``alpha = alpha_init * math.exp(...)`` line of
43	    cognitivecomputations/grokadamw grokadamw.py. We transcribe THAT formula
44	    (max-normalised signal, exp decay), NOT SuperGrok11's train-normalised
45	    variant — the two differ only in the signal denominator and this one is
46	    the published GrokAdamW.
47	  * The fused kernel consumes a SCALAR α per multi-tensor call, so the live
48	    α_t is simply passed through. β1 is per-tensor: until the vector ABI lands
49	    we partition the fused call per tensor (each with its own β1_i); post
50	    rebuild a single call passes the whole β1 vector. See ``step``.
51	
52	All hot-path computation is dispatched to the fused C++/CUDA kernel via _ops.
53	"""
54	
55	import math
56	import warnings
57	from typing import Iterable, Optional, Tuple
58	
59	import torch
60	from torch import Tensor
61	from torch.optim.optimizer import Optimizer
62	
63	from grokking_optimizers.dispatch import get_ops
64	
65	_ops = get_ops()  # Fails loudly if C++ extension not built
66	
67	
68	def _validate_grad(p):
69	    """Validate a gradient before handing its data_ptr to the fused kernel.
70	
71	    The fused kernel indexes raw contiguous memory and dispatches on the
72	    parameter's dtype, so a sparse, dtype-mismatched, or non-contiguous
73	    gradient would silently corrupt the parameter, EMA, and Adam state.
74	    There is no Python fallback, so reject the unsupported cases loudly
75	    and densify the rest.
76	    """
77	    g = p.grad
78	    if g.is_sparse:
79	        raise RuntimeError(
80	            "fused optimizer kernel does not support sparse gradients")
81	    if g.dtype != p.dtype:
82	        raise RuntimeError(
83	            f"grad dtype {g.dtype} != param dtype {p.dtype}; cast gradients "
84	            "to the parameter dtype before step()")
85	    return g if g.is_contiguous() else g.contiguous()
86	
87	
88	@torch.no_grad()
89	def _adamw_step_reference(params, grads, exp_avgs, exp_avg_sqs, steps,
90	                          lr, beta1, beta2, eps, wd):
91	    """Pure-Python AdamW reference step (decoupled weight decay).
92	
93	    Kept as documentation of the math the fused kernel implements; not
94	    invoked on the hot path (the C++ extension's grokadamw_fused_step
95	    handles every GPU/CPU case).
96	    """
97	    for p, g, ea, easq, step in zip(params, grads, exp_avgs, exp_avg_sqs, steps):
98	        bc1 = 1.0 - beta1 ** step
99	        bc2 = 1.0 - beta2 ** step
100	        ea.mul_(beta1).add_(g, alpha=1 - beta1)
101	        easq.mul_(beta2).addcmul_(g, g, value=1 - beta2)
102	        step_size = lr / bc1
103	        denom = (easq / bc2).sqrt().add_(eps)
104	        p.mul_(1 - lr * wd)
105	        p.addcdiv_(ea, denom, value=-step_size)
106

108	class GrokAdamW(Optimizer):
109	    """Adam with grokking-aware EMA gradient filtering and amplification.
110	
111	    Implements the PUBLISHED GrokAdamW (cognitivecomputations/grokadamw):
112	    layer-wise β1 decay + grokking-signal-driven adaptive α (see module
113	    docstring for the transcribed formulas and source lines).
114	
115	    Args:
116	        params: Iterable of parameters or parameter groups.
117	        lr: Learning rate (default: 1e-3).
118	        betas: Coefficients for computing running averages of gradient
119	            and its square (default: (0.9, 0.98)). The reference uses
120	            (0.9, 0.999); we keep our (0.9, 0.98) project default.
121	        eps: Term added to the denominator for numerical stability
122	            (default: 1e-8).
123	        weight_decay: Decoupled weight decay coefficient (default: 1.0).
124	        alpha: ``alpha_init`` — the BASE EMA decay of the slow-grad filter
125	            (default: 0.98). When ``step`` is given both ``train_loss`` and
126	            ``val_loss``, the LIVE decay becomes
127	            ``alpha_t = alpha * exp(-kappa * signal)`` (reference formula).
128	        lamb: Amplification factor applied to the filtered gradient
129	            signal (default: 2.0 — the reference default; was 5.0 historically).
130	        gamma: LAYER-WISE β1 decay rate (WIRED, not deprecated). β1 for the
131	            i-th parameter tensor is ``betas[0] * (1 - gamma) ** i`` (reference
132	            grokadamw.py). gamma=0 ⇒ a single global β1 (identical layers);
133	            gamma>0 ⇒ later layers get less momentum (default: 0.1).
134	        kappa: ``grokking_signal_decay_rate`` — the exponential decay rate of
135	            α vs the grokking signal (reference name; default: 0.1). Only
136	            active when ``step`` receives both train_loss and val_loss.
137	        decay: Back-compat alias accepted but NOT used by the published
138	            algorithm (the reference has no second decay knob). Kept so old
139	            call sites do not break; silently ignored (default: 0.1).
140	        grad_clip: Maximum gradient norm for per-parameter clipping
141	            (default: 1.0).
142	    """
143	
144	    def __init__(
145	        self,
146	        params: Iterable,
147	        lr: float = 1e-3,
148	        betas: Tuple[float, float] = (0.9, 0.98),
149	        eps: float = 1e-8,
150	        weight_decay: float = 1.0,
151	        alpha: float = 0.98,
152	        lamb: float = 2.0,
153	        gamma: float = 0.1,
154	        kappa: float = 0.1,
155	        decay: float = 0.1,
156	        grad_clip: float = 1.0,
157	        use_grad_hooks: bool = False,
158	    ) -> None:
159	        if lr < 0.0:
160	            raise ValueError(f"Invalid learning rate: {lr}")
161	        if eps < 0.0:
162	            raise ValueError(f"Invalid epsilon value: {eps}")
163	        if not isinstance(betas, (tuple, list)) or len(betas) != 2:
164	            raise ValueError(f"Invalid betas (expected a 2-tuple): {betas}")
165	        if not 0.0 <= betas[0] < 1.0:
166	            raise ValueError(f"Invalid beta parameter at index 0: {betas[0]}")
167	        if not 0.0 <= betas[1] < 1.0:
168	            raise ValueError(f"Invalid beta parameter at index 1: {betas[1]}")
169	        if not 0.0 <= alpha < 1.0:
170	            raise ValueError(f"Invalid alpha parameter: {alpha}")
171	        if weight_decay < 0.0:
172	            raise ValueError(f"Invalid weight_decay: {weight_decay}")
173	        if grad_clip <= 0.0:
174	            raise ValueError(f"Invalid grad_clip (must be > 0): {grad_clip}")
175	        if gamma is None:
176	            gamma = 0.0
177	        if not 0.0 <= gamma < 1.0:
178	            raise ValueError(f"Invalid gamma (layer-wise β1 decay, want "
179	                             f"0<=gamma<1): {gamma}")
180	        if kappa is None:
181	            kappa = 0.0
182	        if kappa < 0.0:
183	            raise ValueError(f"Invalid kappa (grokking_signal_decay_rate, want "
184	                             f">=0): {kappa}")
185	        # `decay` is the one remaining back-compat-only arg: the PUBLISHED
186	        # GrokAdamW has no second decay knob, so we accept it and ignore it
187	        # (no DeprecationWarning churn — it simply has no published role).
188	
189	        defaults = dict(
190	            lr=lr,
191	            betas=betas,
192	            eps=eps,
193	            weight_decay=weight_decay,
194	            alpha=alpha,
195	            lamb=lamb,
196	            gamma=gamma,
197	            kappa=kappa,
198	            decay=decay,
199	            grad_clip=grad_clip,
200	        )
201	        super().__init__(params, defaults)
202	
203	        # Per-group cache of static tensor lists (params + exp_avg/exp_avg_sq/ema
204	        # buffers keep a fixed identity across steps); only grads_list and step
205	        # counters are refreshed per step. Invalidated by add_param_group.
206	        self._static_cache: dict = {}
207	        # Lazily-bound fused kernel callable (resolved once at first step()).
208	        self._fused_step = None
209	
210	        # ── Layer-wise β1 (PUBLISHED GrokAdamW): β1_i = β1 * (1 - gamma)**i,
211	        # i the flat enumeration index of the param tensor — the SAME pattern as
212	        # supergrok11.py::_flat_layer_beta1s. Precompute the per-param-id β1 so
213	        # the hot path is a dict lookup. Index runs across ALL groups (global
214	        # layer order), matching the reference's single enumerate(params).
215	        self._layer_beta1_by_id: dict = {}
216	        idx = 0
217	        for group in self.param_groups:
218	            beta1 = group["betas"][0]
219	            g_gamma = group["gamma"]
220	            for p in group["params"]:
221	                self._layer_beta1_by_id[id(p)] = beta1 * ((1.0 - g_gamma) ** idx)
222	                idx += 1
223	
224	        # Grokking signal (one scalar per step — the reference computes a single
225	        # train/val signal shared across groups) and whether it has ever been
226	        # set. α is derived PER GROUP from it (alpha_init & kappa are group-level
227	        # in the reference), so we keep the signal, not a pre-baked α.
228	        self._grok_signal: float = 0.0
229	        self._signal_active: bool = False
230	
231	        self._use_grad_hooks = use_grad_hooks
232	        if use_grad_hooks:
233	            _register_grad_hooks(self)
234	
235	    def _layer_beta1(self, p) -> float:
236	        """Per-tensor β1 (= β1 * (1-gamma)**layer_index). Falls back to the
237	        group β1 for a param added after construction (defensive: a freshly
238	        ``add_param_group``'d tensor not yet indexed gets gamma^0 = full β1)."""
239	        return self._layer_beta1_by_id.get(
240	            id(p), self.param_groups[0]["betas"][0])
241	
242	    @staticmethod
243	    def _grokking_signal(train_loss, val_loss) -> float:
244	        """Reference _default_grokking_signal (max-normalised clipped gap):
245	            diff = max(0, val - train); m = max(val, train); signal = diff/m.
246	        Returns 0.0 if either loss is None or m<=0."""
247	        if train_loss is None or val_loss is None:
248	            return 0.0
249	        diff = max(0.0, float(val_loss) - float(train_loss))
250	        max_loss = max(float(val_loss), float(train_loss))
251	        return diff / max_loss if max_loss > 0.0 else 0.0
252	
253	    def _alpha_for_group(self, group) -> float:
254	        """Live α_t for a group (PUBLISHED GrokAdamW, per group):
255	            α = alpha_init * exp(-kappa * signal).
256	        Until a (train_loss, val_loss) pair has ever been supplied, returns the
257	        group's alpha_init unchanged. alpha_init == group["alpha"] and
258	        kappa == group["kappa"] (grokking_signal_decay_rate)."""
259	        if not self._signal_active:
260	            return group["alpha"]
261	        return group["alpha"] * math.exp(-group["kappa"] * self._grok_signal)
262	
263	    def add_param_group(self, param_group) -> None:
264	        self._static_cache = {}
265	        super().add_param_group(param_group)
266	        # Layer indices shift when a group is appended, so recompute the
267	        # per-param-id β1 across ALL groups (global enumeration order).
268	        self._layer_beta1_by_id = {}
269	        idx = 0
270	        for group in self.param_groups:
271	            beta1 = group["betas"][0]
272	            g_gamma = group["gamma"]
273	            for p in group["params"]:
274	                self._layer_beta1_by_id[id(p)] = beta1 * ((1.0 - g_gamma) ** idx)
275	                idx += 1
276	
277	    def _group_cache(self, group, grads_by_id):
278	        """Return cached (params, exp_avg, exp_avg_sq, ema, states).
279	
280	        Keyed on the grad-bearing param ids. ``grads_by_id`` provides the
281	        first-gradient EMA seed on first init."""
282	        key = tuple(id(p) for p in group["params"] if p.grad is not None)
283	        cached = self._static_cache.get(id(group))
284	        if cached is not None and cached[0] == key:
285	            return cached[1]
286	
287	        params_list = []
288	        exp_avg_list = []
289	        exp_avg_sq_list = []
290	        ema_list = []
291	        states = []
292	        for p in group["params"]:
293	            if p.grad is None:
294	                continue
295	            state = self.state[p]
296	            if len(state) == 0:
297	                state["step"] = 0
298	                state["exp_avg"] = torch.zeros_like(p, dtype=torch.float32)
299	                state["exp_avg_sq"] = torch.zeros_like(p, dtype=torch.float32)
300	                # Seed the gradient EMA with the first gradient (not zeros) —
301	                # see Grokfast; a zero seed under-amplifies the early grokking
302	                # phase and the kernel applies no EMA bias correction.
303	                state["ema"] = grads_by_id[id(p)].detach().to(
304	                    torch.float32).clone()
305	            params_list.append(p)
306	            exp_avg_list.append(state["exp_avg"])
307	            exp_avg_sq_list.append(state["exp_avg_sq"])
308	            ema_list.append(state["ema"])
309	            states.append(state)
310	        entry = (params_list, exp_avg_list, exp_avg_sq_list, ema_list, states)
311	        self._static_cache[id(group)] = (key, entry)
312	        return entry
313	
314	    @torch.no_grad()
315	    def step(self, closure=None, train_loss=None, val_loss=None
316	             ) -> Optional[float]:
317	        """Perform a single optimisation step.
318	
319	        Args:
320	            closure: A closure that re-evaluates the model and returns the loss
321	                (optional).
322	            train_loss: Current training loss (scalar / float). When BOTH this
323	                and ``val_loss`` are given, the live grokking signal is
324	                recomputed and α_t = alpha_init * exp(-kappa * signal) drives the
325	                slow-grad EMA decay this step (PUBLISHED GrokAdamW). Pass them on
326	                the cadence the caller wants α to adapt; on steps where either is
327	                None, α stays at its previous value (alpha_init on the first).
328	            val_loss: Current validation/eval loss (scalar / float).
329	
330	        Returns:
331	            The loss value if *closure* is provided, otherwise ``None``.
332	        """
333	        loss = None
334	        if closure is not None:
335	            with torch.enable_grad():
336	                loss = closure()
337	
338	        # Grokking-signal → live α_t (reference: alpha = alpha_init *
339	        # exp(-grokking_signal_decay_rate * signal), applied per group in
340	        # _alpha_for_group). Only recomputes when BOTH losses are supplied;
341	        # otherwise the last signal carries over (and α stays at alpha_init until
342	        # the first pair arrives).
343	        if train_loss is not None and val_loss is not None:
344	            self._grok_signal = self._grokking_signal(train_loss, val_loss)
345	            self._signal_active = True
346	
347	        if self._use_grad_hooks:
348	            return loss
349	
350	        # Bind the resolved kernel callable once on the instance, then reuse it
351	        # across steps instead of going through the _LazyOps proxy each step.
352	        fused_step = self._fused_step
353	        if fused_step is None:
354	            fused_step = self._fused_step = _ops.bind("grokadamw_fused_step")
355	
356	        for group in self.param_groups:
357	            grads_by_id = {
358	                id(p): _validate_grad(p)
359	                for p in group["params"] if p.grad is not None
360	            }
361	            params_list, exp_avg_list, exp_avg_sq_list, ema_list, states = \
362	                self._group_cache(group, grads_by_id)
363	
364	            if len(params_list) == 0:
365	                continue
366	
367	            grads_list = [grads_by_id[id(p)] for p in params_list]
368	            step_list = []
369	            for state in states:
370	                state["step"] += 1
371	                step_list.append(state["step"])
372	
373	            # Live α_t (group alpha_init if no signal yet) — a SCALAR the kernel
374	            # accepts as-is. β1 is PER-TENSOR (layer-wise decay), so it must vary
375	            # per param: β1_i = β1*(1-gamma)**layer_index.
376	            alpha_t = self._alpha_for_group(group)
377	            beta1s = [self._layer_beta1(p) for p in params_list]
378	
379	            self._dispatch_grokadamw(
380	                fused_step, params_list, grads_list, exp_avg_list,
381	                exp_avg_sq_list, ema_list, step_list, alpha_t, beta1s, group)
382	
383	        return loss
384	
385	    # Has the rebuilt extension grown the vector-β1 ABI? None = unprobed;
386	    # True/False latched after the first attempt so we don't re-raise/re-catch
387	    # the TypeError every step. Class-level so all instances share the verdict.
388	    _vector_beta1_abi: Optional[bool] = None
389	
390	    def _dispatch_grokadamw(self, fused_step, params_list, grads_list,
391	                            exp_avg_list, exp_avg_sq_list, ema_list, step_list,
392	                            alpha_t, beta1s, group):
393	        """Drive the fused GrokAdamW kernel with a live scalar α_t and a
394	        PER-TENSOR β1 vector (layer-wise decay).
395	
396	        Two paths, selected by an ABI probe (stale-ABI latch):
397	          • VECTOR ABI (post-rebuild): the C++ ``grokadamw_fused_step`` accepts a
398	            ``layer_beta1s`` vector after ``steps`` — ONE multi-tensor launch
399	            passes the whole β1 vector + scalar α_t. Faithful and fastest.
400	          • INTERIM (no rebuild): the shipped binding takes a SCALAR β1, so we
401	            PARTITION the params by their β1_i value and issue one fused call per
402	            distinct β1 (each its own scalar β1 + the live α_t). Correctness over
403	            launch count until the ABI lands. With gamma=0 every β1_i is equal ⇒
404	            exactly one call (no regression vs the old single-call path)."""
405	        cls = type(self)
406	        if cls._vector_beta1_abi is not False:
407	            # Try the new signature: layer_beta1s inserted right after steps.
408	            try:
409	                fused_step(
410	                    params_list, grads_list, exp_avg_list, exp_avg_sq_list,
411	                    ema_list, step_list, beta1s,
412	                    alpha_t, group["lamb"], group["betas"][0],
413	                    group["betas"][1], group["lr"], group["weight_decay"],
414	                    group["eps"], group["grad_clip"],
415	                )
416	                if cls._vector_beta1_abi is None:
417	                    cls._vector_beta1_abi = True
418	                return
419	            except TypeError:
420	                if cls._vector_beta1_abi is None:
421	                    cls._vector_beta1_abi = False
422	                    warnings.warn(
423	                        "GrokAdamW: the compiled extension does not yet expose "
424	                        "the vector-β1 grokadamw_fused_step ABI; using the "
425	                        "interim per-β1 partitioned launch (correct, slightly "
426	                        "more launches). Rebuild (`pip install -e .`) to get the "
427	                        "single-call vector path.", RuntimeWarning, stacklevel=2)
428	                # fall through to the interim partitioned path
429	        self._dispatch_partitioned(
430	            fused_step, params_list, grads_list, exp_avg_list, exp_avg_sq_list,
431	            ema_list, step_list, alpha_t, beta1s, group)
432	
433	    @staticmethod
434	    def _dispatch_partitioned(fused_step, params_list, grads_list, exp_avg_list,
435	                              exp_avg_sq_list, ema_list, step_list, alpha_t,
436	                              beta1s, group):
437	        """Interim path: group tensors by identical β1_i and issue one scalar-β1
438	        fused call per group (each passing the live scalar α_t)."""
439	        # Bucket indices by their β1 value (preserve first-seen order).
440	        buckets: dict = {}
441	        order = []
442	        for i, b1 in enumerate(beta1s):
443	            if b1 not in buckets:
444	                buckets[b1] = []
445	                order.append(b1)
446	            buckets[b1].append(i)
447	        for b1 in order:
448	            idxs = buckets[b1]
449	            fused_step(
450	                [params_list[i] for i in idxs],
451	                [grads_list[i] for i in idxs],
452	                [exp_avg_list[i] for i in idxs],
453	                [exp_avg_sq_list[i] for i in idxs],
454	                [ema_list[i] for i in idxs],
455	                [step_list[i] for i in idxs],
456	                alpha_t, group["lamb"], b1, group["betas"][1],
457	                group["lr"], group["weight_decay"], group["eps"],
458	                group["grad_clip"],
459	            )
460	
461	    def _single_param_step(self, param, group, state):
462	        """Per-parameter step used by the `use_grad_hooks=True` path.
463	
464	        Uses this param's LAYER-WISE β1 and the live α_t (updated by step() from
465	        the grokking signal). Routed through the SAME ABI-probed dispatcher as
466	        the batched path so it is correct both pre- and post-rebuild."""
467	        if param.grad is None:
468	            return
469	        grad = _validate_grad(param)
470	        if len(state) == 0:
471	            state["step"] = 0
472	            state["exp_avg"] = torch.zeros_like(param, dtype=torch.float32)
473	            state["exp_avg_sq"] = torch.zeros_like(param, dtype=torch.float32)
474	            state["ema"] = grad.detach().to(torch.float32).clone()
475	        state["step"] += 1
476	        fused_step = self._fused_step
477	        if fused_step is None:
478	            fused_step = self._fused_step = _ops.bind("grokadamw_fused_step")
479	        self._dispatch_grokadamw(
480	            fused_step, [param], [grad], [state["exp_avg"]],
481	            [state["exp_avg_sq"]], [state["ema"]], [state["step"]],
482	            self._alpha_for_group(group), [self._layer_beta1(param)], group)
483	
484	
485	# ── Shared (inlined) helper: register post_accumulate_grad_hook on each param.
486	# Each hook calls back into the optimizer's `_single_param_step` so the update
487	# runs while gradient data is still L2-warm. Duplicated across every optimizer
488	# file by design (self-containment); requires PyTorch >= 2.1.
489	def _register_grad_hooks(optimizer):
490	    _pt = tuple(int(x) for x in torch.__version__.split("+")[0].split(".")[:2])
491	    if _pt < (2, 1):
492	        raise RuntimeError(
493	            f"use_grad_hooks requires PyTorch >= 2.1 for "
494	            f"register_post_accumulate_grad_hook. Current: {torch.__version__}.")
495	    optimizer._grad_hook_handles = []
496	    for group in optimizer.param_groups:
497	        for p in group["params"]:
498	            if not p.requires_grad:
499	                continue
500	            def _hook(param, _g=group, _opt=optimizer):
501	                if param.grad is None:
502	                    return
503	                _opt._single_param_step(param, _g, _opt.state[param])
504	            optimizer._grad_hook_handles.append(
505	                p.register_post_accumulate_grad_hook(_hook))

102	    # grad_clip and _opt_scalars_from forwards grokfast_alpha/lamb, so the live
103	    # optimizer's full mechanism reaches the tail.
104	    "grokfast/decoder": dict(model="decoder", opt="grokfast", factory=_grokfast_factory),

135	def _build_cell(model, seed=42):
136	    """Build the live race model + one real batch + the L3-REAL flat layout.
137	
138	    DETERMINISM (load-bearing for gate 2): build_model does NOT reseed from
139	    c["seed"] internally — it draws from the global RNG — so the A/A/A determinism
140	    check MUST reseed here, or each rebuild yields different random init weights and
141	    the gate would compare runs with DIFFERENT inputs (a test bug, not kernel
142	    non-determinism). We torch.manual_seed(seed) immediately before build_model so
143	    every _build_cell(model, seed) returns byte-identical initial params."""
144	    g = _g()
145	    c = dict(g.DEFAULT_CONFIG)
146	    c.update({"model_type": model, "use_amp": False, "use_fused": True,
147	              "compile_model": False, "matmul_precision": "bf16", "seed": seed,
148	              "frac_train": 0.5, "val_ratio": 0.10, "p": 97})
149	    dev = torch.device("cuda")
150	    data = tuple(d.to(dev) for d in g.make_data_for_task(c, seed))
151	    torch.manual_seed(seed)            # pin build_model's global-RNG draw
152	    torch.cuda.manual_seed_all(seed)
153	    m = g.build_model(c, dev)
154	    return g, c, m, data, dev

157	def run_cell_gate(cell_key, verbose=True):
158	    """Run gates (1)+(2) for one converted cell. Returns (ok, detail)."""
159	    from grokking_optimizers.dispatch import (has_l3_real, gemm_impl_for_cell,
160	                                              canonicalize_model, fused_train_step)
161	    spec = _CELLS[cell_key]
162	    model, opt = spec["model"], spec["opt"]
163	    g, c, m, data, dev = _build_cell(model)
164	    canon = canonicalize_model(model)
165	    # Precondition: the cell must actually be wired L3-TC (wgmma) — else the gate is
166	    # meaningless. has_l3_real + gemm_impl_for_cell are the production gates.
167	    assert has_l3_real(canon, opt), f"{cell_key}: not L3-REAL (wire it first)"
168	    eng = gemm_impl_for_cell(canon, opt, "bf16")
169	    assert eng == "wgmma", f"{cell_key}: bf16 engine is {eng!r}, expected wgmma"
170	
171	    tx, ty = data[0], data[1]
172	    # A live optimizer carrying the EXACT production hyperparameters (drives the
173	    # kernel's scalars via _opt_scalars_from inside fused_train_step).
174	    opt_obj = spec["factory"](g, m.parameters(), c)
175	
176	    # Snapshot the initial flat params (named_parameters order) BEFORE the step.
